epics.title: E09 — Systemic Stealth
epics.description:
## Outcome
Visibility, lighting, sound, suspicion, searching, last-known-position and hiding work as coherent, deterministic systems. Stealth is not crouching + an eye icon: players read light exposure, noise and each enemy’s awareness, and failure escalates into new situations rather than a reload.

## Scope
- In: visibility model (light, stance, motion, distance, contrast), multi-point LOS with partial cover, sound propagation through rooms/doors/walls/floors, surface acoustics and footsteps, verticality rules, hiding places, anomaly detection, stealth HUD and directional awareness indicators, LKP ghost, text barks/stingers, zone alarm escalation, stealth tuning data, stealth grey-box course, deterministic infiltration scenario suite, assists.
- Out: thief verbs (mw-e10), AI state machine and behaviours (mw-e11), creature data (mw-e12), final art/audio (E37/E38 asset beads), crime/bounty systems.

## Exit criteria
- Stealth rules in `src/sim` at 100% coverage.
- ≥ 10 infiltration replay scenarios green and deterministic.
- Stealth grey-box course playable end-to-end in the browser.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the infiltration scenario suite, when run in CI, then all scenarios pass with identical state-hash sequences across two runs.
- EC-2 [unit] Given coverage reports, when CI runs, then stealth modules in `src/sim` report 100% lines/branches/functions/statements.
- EC-3 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when a scripted player completes it undetected and once detected-then-escaped, then both runs finish without errors.
- EC-4 [manual] Given 5 playtesters, when asked why they were detected, then ≥ 4 of 5 can name the cause (light, noise, anomaly).

epics.title: E10 — Thief Toolkit
epics.description:
## Outcome
Lockpicking, pickpocketing, thrown distractions, extinguishing lights, climbing, hiding bodies, disguises, silent movement, takedowns, traps and escape tools produce a complete thief fantasy built on shared world systems (properties, light, sound, AI perception).

## Scope
- In: thief tool item data, distractions, light extinguishing, takedowns (lethal/non-lethal), body carry/hide, lockpicking (spike + in-world implementation), pickpocketing/planting, climbing + ropes, disguises, trap placement and disarming, smoke/flash escapes, silent-movement capability unlocks, lean/peek, environmental takedowns, grey-box thief vault challenge.
- Out: stealth simulation core (mw-e09), AI (mw-e11), progression UI (E19), loot/shop placement (E18/E20), final art/animation.

## Exit criteria
- Thief vault challenge solvable by ≥ 3 scripted routes plus one failure-and-escape route.
- Every thief verb interacts through properties, not item-specific scripts.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the thief vault challenge, when each scripted route runs, then all complete deterministically.
- EC-2 [unit] Given thief rule modules, when coverage runs, then `src/sim` coverage is 100%.
- EC-3 [manual] Given 3 playtesters, when completing an undetected infiltration, then ≥ 2 rate it at least as satisfying as a hard fight (≥ 4/5).

epics.title: E11 — Enemy AI
epics.description:
## Outcome
Enemies patrol, perceive, investigate, communicate, fight, retreat, search and return to believable routines through a deterministic, data-driven behaviour runtime and the six-state alert machine (Unaware → Suspicious → Investigating → Searching → Alerted → Combat). Enemies never know the player position except through their senses.

## Scope
- In: architecture spike + runtime, scenario test harness, navigation, perception, awareness, alert states, memory/LKP, patrol, investigate, search, communication/alarms, combat, retreat/flee, return to routine, AI tuning data, debug visualisation, AI perf budget.
- Out: creature data schema (mw-e12), stealth inputs (mw-e09), boss/bestiary-specific behaviours (E13/E26), social dialogue (E14/E22).

## Exit criteria
- Grey-box fight (m1) uses this AI; stealth scenarios (m2) pass.
- No-omniscience enforced by architecture tests.
- 24 agents within the AI perf budget.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [unit] Given the AI modules, when an architecture test scans imports, then no behaviour/memory module reads ground-truth player transforms.
- EC-2 [perf] Given the AI stress scene, when run on the reference machine, then AI+perception+sound cost p95 ≤ 3 ms per tick.
- EC-3 [integration] Given the AI scenario suite, when run, then every scenario is deterministic and green.
- EC-4 [e2e] Given the grey-box fight room, when the player fights fixture guards, then guards patrol, detect, fight and search without errors.

epics.title: E12 — Creature Framework
epics.description:
## Outcome
Creatures are data: unique senses, locomotion, attacks, property-driven vulnerabilities, factions/relationships, dispositions, fears/morale, personalities, needs and non-hostile interaction affordances are all declared in validated content and consumed by AI and stealth systems — ready for the bestiary (E13) and social creatures (E14).

## Scope
- In: creature schema, sense profiles, grey-box fixtures, spawner, attack definitions, locomotion, vulnerabilities via world properties, factions, dispositions, fears/morale, personality traits, needs hooks, interaction affordances, creature save state, auto smoke-test harness, authoring guide.
- Out: specific bestiary creatures (E13), social creature content and dialogue (E14/E22), final models/animations (E37 asset beads).

## Exit criteria
- A new creature can be added with data only and passes the auto smoke harness.
- Schemas and runtime at 100% coverage.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [content] Given any creature data file, when validated and smoke-tested, then it passes with no code changes required.
- EC-2 [unit] Given creature modules, when coverage runs, then `src/sim` and `src/content` creature code is at 100%.
- EC-3 [manual] Given the authoring guide, when a designer follows it, then a new creature is added in ≤ 30 min.

items.title: Define zod creature schema with senses, locomotion, attacks and needs
items.description:
## Why
The constitution says enemies are creatures, not target dummies, and creatures must be data-driven. Every AI, stealth and bestiary feature needs one shared, validated creature definition.

## What
A `CreatureDef` zod schema in `src/content/schemas/creature.ts` with typed sections: `id`, `family`, `tags`, `stats` (health, poise, mass, size class), `senses` (ref to sense profile or inline), `locomotion` (list of locomotion modes), `attacks` (list of attack refs), `properties` (world-property tags such as `flammable`, `undead`, `conductive`), `vulnerabilities`/`resistances`, `faction`, `disposition` defaults, `fears`, `personality`, `needs`, `behaviour` (behaviour profile id + tuning overrides), `interactions` (non-hostile affordances), `loot` ref, `presentation` (placeholder mesh id, sfx set id). Every section except `id`, `family`, `stats`, `senses`, `locomotion` is optional with documented defaults. A loader registers creatures into the content registry and resolves refs.

## Scope
- In: Schema, TypeScript types inferred from zod, ref resolution, default filling
- In: Clear validation errors naming the file and JSON path
- In: Schema version field for future migrations
- Out: Specific creatures (E13 Bestiary / world-content group)
- Out: Runtime behaviour for each section — later E12/E11 items consume the fields
- Out: Dialogue content (E22/E14)

## Notes
Section sub-schemas are owned by later items (e12-sense-profiles, e12-locomotion-types, e12-attack-definitions, …); this item creates the envelope with stub sub-schemas they extend. Keep refs string-typed (`attack:goblin-slash`) and resolved at load. Related: E13 Bestiary and E14 Social Creatures consume this schema.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given a creature file containing only `id`, `family`, `stats`, `senses` and `locomotion`, when validated, then it passes and all optional sections are filled with the documented defaults.
- AC-2 [content] Given a creature file missing `stats.health`, when validated, then validation fails with an error message containing the file path and `stats.health`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature referencing `attack:does-not-exist`, when the content registry resolves refs, then loading fails listing every unresolved ref (not just the first).
- AC-4 [unit] Given two creature files with the same `id`, when loaded, then loading fails with a duplicate-id error naming both files.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a valid creature def, when round-tripped through serialize → parse, then the result deep-equals the input.
- AC-6 [content] Given the schema, when `pnpm content:docs` runs, then a field reference table is generated at `docs/content/creature-schema.md` with every field, type and default.

items.title: Add sense profile data: sight cones, hearing, smell, special senses
items.description:
## Why
Creatures should perceive differently — a spider feels vibration, a wraith senses life, a goblin sees in the dark. Unique senses make stealth a puzzle rather than one global rule.

## What
A `SenseProfile` sub-schema and data files: `sight` (near/far range m, primary and peripheral half-angles, vertical half-angle, dark-vision factor 0–1, detection speed multiplier), `hearing` (sensitivity dB threshold, range cap), `smell` (range m, wind-sensitivity flag, tracks scent trails flag), and extensible `special` senses (`tremor`, `life-sense`, `magic-sense`) each with range and gating properties. Profiles are reusable (`senses: "sense:humanoid-guard"`) and overridable per creature.

## Scope
- In: Sub-schema + validation
- In: Three baseline profiles used by test fixtures: humanoid, beast, undead
- In: Merge semantics for per-creature overrides
- Out: Runtime evaluation of senses (e11-perception)
- Out: Smell trail simulation beyond hooks (post-MVP)

## Notes
Units are metres, degrees and seconds everywhere. Special senses are declared as data with a `channel` name so e11-perception can register handlers without schema changes.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given a sense profile with `sight.primaryHalfAngle` greater than `sight.peripheralHalfAngle`, when validated, then validation fails with a message naming both fields.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature referencing `sense:humanoid` and overriding `sight.farRange: 30`, when resolved, then far range is 30 and every other sight field equals the base profile.
- AC-3 [content] Given the baseline humanoid profile, when validated, then it defines sight far range between 15 and 30 m and hearing threshold between 20 and 40 dB (documented tuning band).
- AC-4 [content] Given a profile declaring an unknown special sense channel, when validated, then validation fails listing the registered channels.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a profile with negative range values, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Author three grey-box creature fixtures for AI and stealth tests
items.description:
## Why
AI and stealth tests need stable, deliberately boring creatures that are not bestiary content so tuning the real bestiary never breaks rule tests.

## What
Three test-fixture creature defs in `src/content/fixtures/creatures/`: `fixture-guard` (humanoid, sight-dominant, patrols, can communicate), `fixture-hound` (beast, hearing + smell dominant, fast), `fixture-sentinel` (undead, life-sense, never sleeps, ignores darkness). Each uses placeholder capsule meshes and the baseline sense profiles.

## Scope
- In: Fixture data + README explaining that fixtures are frozen for tests
- In: Excluded from shipping content bundles
- Out: Real bestiary creatures (E13)
- Out: Art (capsules only)

## Notes
Changing fixture values requires updating dependent scenario tests; add a header comment saying so.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the three fixture files, when validated against `CreatureDef`, then all pass.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a production content build, when bundled, then no fixture creature id appears in the output manifest.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `fixture-sentinel`, when its resolved senses are inspected, then dark-vision factor is 1.0 and it declares the `life-sense` channel.
- AC-4 [content] Given each fixture, when its content smoke test runs, then it spawns, ticks 600 sim frames without error and despawns.

items.title: Spawn data-defined creatures into the sim and grey-box scenes
items.description:
## Why
Designers and tests must be able to put any creature into the world from data alone, fast.

## What
As a designer, I want to spawn any creature by id at a position (from level data, debug console or tests) so that I can iterate on encounters without code. The spawner builds the entity/component set from a resolved `CreatureDef` (transform, health, senses, locomotion, behaviour, faction, needs), binds a placeholder capsule render proxy in `src/game`, and supports despawn and respawn. Debug console: `spawn <creatureId> [count] [at-cursor]`, `despawn all`.

## Scope
- In: Sim-side factory (pure) + game-side render binding
- In: Level-data spawn points with optional patrol route and faction override
- In: Console commands
- Out: Spawn waves / encounter director (E26 content)
- Out: Final meshes (asset integration beads)

## Notes
Factory must be deterministic: entity ids allocated from the sim entity store, any per-spawn variance from seeded RNG.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given `fixture-guard` and a seed, when spawned twice in fresh sims with the same seed, then both entity component snapshots hash identically.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an unknown creature id, when spawn is requested, then no entity is created and a typed `SpawnError` is returned (sim does not throw).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the grey-box testbed, when `spawn fixture-hound 3` is run in the debug console, then 3 hound entities exist with render proxies within 1 frame.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a spawn point with a faction override, when spawned, then the entity faction equals the override, not the def default.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the grey-box testbed, when a level with 4 spawn points loads, then 4 creatures are visible and the console shows no errors.

items.title: Data-driven creature attack definitions bound to the damage model
items.description:
## Why
Combat is intrinsically fun only when attacks are readable and varied; creatures need telegraphed, data-defined attacks that behave consistently with player combat.

## What
An `AttackDef` schema: id, kind (`melee` | `projectile` | `area` | `grab` | `special`), range min/max m, windup/active/recovery frames, telegraph cue id, hitbox shape ref, damage packets (type + amount + poise), cooldown s, selection weight, preconditions (distance, target stance, own health band). A sim executor runs an attack’s phases and emits hitbox activations to the damage model.

## Scope
- In: Schema + executor for melee and projectile kinds
- In: Telegraph events for render/audio to consume
- In: Preconditions evaluated deterministically
- Out: Choosing which attack to use (e11-combat-behaviour)
- Out: Grab/special runtime beyond a stub event (post-MVP or bestiary items)

## Notes
Frame counts are in fixed sim ticks. Telegraph cues are string ids so placeholder sfx/vfx can be swapped later.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a melee attack with windup 12, active 4, recovery 10 ticks, when executed, then the hitbox is active exactly on ticks 13–16 and the attack completes on tick 26.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an attack executing, when the attacker is staggered during windup, then the attack is cancelled and no hitbox activates.
- AC-3 [content] Given an attack with `range.min` > `range.max`, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a telegraph cue id, when windup starts, then exactly one `AttackTelegraph` event is emitted on the event bus with the attacker id and cue id.
- AC-5 [integration] Given `fixture-guard` attacking a player hurtbox in range, when the active window overlaps, then the damage model receives one damage packet per packet definition.

items.title: Support walker, climber, flier, swimmer and burrower locomotion data
items.description:
## Why
Verticality and alternate routes only matter if creatures move differently: a spider on the ceiling, a harpy over a chasm, a hound that cannot climb.

## What
A `LocomotionMode` schema (`walk`, `climb`, `fly`, `swim`, `burrow`, `wallcrawl`) with speeds per gait (sneak/walk/run), step height, jump height, max slope, and nav-area permissions. Creatures list one or more modes; the navigation layer receives a per-creature nav capability mask derived from them.

## Scope
- In: Schema + capability mask derivation
- In: Gait speeds used by patrol/investigate/combat
- In: Area-cost multipliers (e.g. swimmer prefers water)
- Out: Navmesh generation itself (e11-navigation)
- Out: Flight physics beyond kinematic movement (post-MVP)

## Notes
Mask is a bitfield so nav queries stay cheap. Mode transitions (walk→climb) are nav link types.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with only `walk`, when its capability mask is derived, then `climb`, `fly` and `swim` bits are 0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature with `walk` and `climb`, when the mask is derived, then climb-only nav links are traversable for it and not for a walk-only creature.
- AC-3 [content] Given a locomotion entry with `run` speed lower than `walk` speed, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature with no locomotion modes, when validated, then validation fails (every creature must move or declare `stationary`).

items.title: Drive creature vulnerabilities from world properties, not pairings
items.description:
## Why
The constitution requires systemic interactions: a creature tagged `flammable` should burn from any fire source, and `undead` should respond to any light effect, without scripted spell/creature pairs.

## What
As a player, I want creatures to react to the same world properties as objects so that my experiments transfer. Creatures carry world-property tags (from e03-world-properties) plus `vulnerabilities`/`resistances` keyed by damage type or property effect (e.g. `heat: x2`, `frozen: immune`, `light: stagger`). A sim rule applies element-propagation effects to creatures exactly as to objects, then applies the creature multiplier.

## Scope
- In: Property tags on creatures participate in element propagation
- In: Multiplier + immunity + special reaction (stagger, flee trigger) data
- In: Resolution order documented
- Out: New element types (E03)
- Out: Specific creature weaknesses (E13)

## Notes
Express everything as properties; tests must use property names, never spell names. Reactions can emit a `FearStimulus` consumed by e12-fears-morale.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any creature tagged `flammable` inside an active fire volume, when 1 s of sim time passes, then it gains the `burning` state.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature with `resistances.heat: immune`, when inside a fire volume, then it takes 0 heat damage and does not gain `burning`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature with `vulnerabilities.cold: 2.0`, when it receives a 10-point cold packet, then it loses 20 health.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature with reaction `light: stagger` and light level at its position rising above the configured threshold within 1 tick, then it enters stagger once and not again until light falls below the threshold (no re-trigger spam).
- AC-5 [content] Given a vulnerability keyed by an unknown property or damage type, when validated, then validation fails listing known keys.

items.title: Faction table and relationship queries between creatures
items.description:
## Why
Goblins that fight skeletons, wolves that avoid trolls and guards that tolerate a disguised thief all need one relationship model.

## What
Faction data (`factions.json`): id, default stance toward each other faction (`ally`, `friendly`, `neutral`, `wary`, `hostile`, `prey`, `predator`) and toward the player. Runtime API `relation(a, b)` combining faction stance, per-creature overrides and dynamic modifiers (e.g. the player attacked this faction). Relationship changes emit events.

## Scope
- In: Faction schema + symmetric/asymmetric stances
- In: Dynamic faction-wide modifiers stored in sim state (save-compatible)
- In: Query API used by perception/alert/combat
- Out: Individual disposition toward player (e12-dispositions)
- Out: Story-specific factions (E39/E13 content)

## Notes
Asymmetry is allowed (wolves see sheep as prey; sheep see wolves as predator).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given faction A hostile to B, when `relation(a, b)` is queried for members, then it returns `hostile`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an asymmetric definition A→B `prey` and B→A `predator`, when queried both ways, then each direction returns its own stance.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature-level override making one member of A friendly to the player, when queried, then that creature returns `friendly` and other A members keep the faction default.
- AC-4 [content] Given a faction referencing an undefined faction id, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the player kills a member of faction A witnessed by another A member, when the rule runs, then A’s dynamic stance toward the player worsens one step and a `FactionRelationChanged` event is emitted once.

items.title: Per-creature disposition toward the player with event modifiers
items.description:
## Why
Some creatures can be tricked, helped, befriended or angered; that needs a persistent per-individual attitude, not just a faction flag.

## What
Disposition value −100..100 per creature toward the player, seeded from def + faction. Data-driven modifier rules map sim events to deltas (`attacked: -40`, `fed: +15`, `witnessed-theft: -20`, `helped-ally: +25`). Thresholds map to stances (hostile < −50 ≤ wary < −10 ≤ neutral ≤ 10 < friendly ≤ 50 < devoted). Decay toward baseline is optional per creature.

## Scope
- In: Runtime value, modifier rules, thresholds, decay
- In: Events for UI/dialogue to consume
- In: Save serialization of values
- Out: Dialogue conditions using disposition (e22-dialogue-runtime)
- Out: Social creature content (E14)

## Notes
Modifier rules are content data so E14 can add new event types without code changes.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature at disposition 0, when the player attacks it, then disposition becomes −40 and stance becomes `wary`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given disposition 95, when a +15 modifier applies, then it clamps to 100.
- AC-3 [unit] Given decay rate 1/min toward baseline 0, when 10 sim minutes pass from 20, then disposition is 10.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a modifier rule for an event type that never fires, when the sim runs 10,000 ticks, then disposition is unchanged (no drift).
- AC-5 [integration] Given a saved game with a creature at −37, when loaded, then disposition is exactly −37.

items.title: Creature fears and morale that trigger fleeing and cowering
items.description:
## Why
Creatures have fears. Frightening a wolf pack with fire or breaking goblin morale by felling their leader are non-lethal solutions the constitution wants.

## What
As a player, I want to exploit what creatures fear so that I can win encounters without killing everything. `fears`: list of {stimulus property or faction or event, intensity}. Morale 0–100 per creature, reduced by fear stimuli, ally deaths, low health, leader death; restored over time and near allies. Below thresholds the creature emits `Cower` or `Flee` intents for the AI.

## Scope
- In: Fear stimulus matching via properties (e.g. anything `burning` or light level > X)
- In: Morale model + thresholds + recovery
- In: Group morale shock when a `leader`-tagged ally dies
- Out: Flee movement behaviour (e11-retreat-flee)
- Out: Intimidation dialogue (E14)

## Notes
Fear stimuli are perceived — the creature must sense the burning object (via e11-perception) for it to count.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with fear {property `burning`, intensity 30} and morale 50, when it perceives a burning object within 5 m, then morale drops to 20 and a `Flee` intent is emitted (flee threshold 25).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fear stimulus the creature cannot perceive (behind a wall), when evaluated, then morale is unchanged.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a `leader`-tagged creature dies, when allies within 20 m perceive it, then each ally loses the configured leader-shock morale once.
- AC-4 [unit] Given morale 10 and no stimuli, when 30 s pass near 2 allies, then morale recovers by the configured rate and the `Flee` intent clears once above 35 (hysteresis).
- AC-5 [content] Given a fear with intensity outside 0–100, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Personality traits that weight AI decisions per individual
items.description:
## Why
Personalities make creatures memorable: a lazy guard who gives up searching early, a curious goblin who investigates every noise.

## What
Trait vector (bravery, curiosity, aggression, diligence, sociability, greed) 0–1 per creature, def default plus seeded per-spawn jitter within a declared range. Traits are exposed as inputs to the behaviour runtime (utility weights or BT conditions) and to tuning curves (e.g. diligence scales search duration).

## Scope
- In: Schema, deterministic jitter, accessor API
- In: Documented list of which AI behaviours read which trait
- Out: Dialogue personality/voice (E22)
- Out: Named-character authored personalities (E13/E14 content)

## Notes
Jitter must come from the seeded sim RNG keyed by entity id so replays match.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a def with curiosity 0.5 ± 0.2, when 1,000 spawns are sampled with a fixed seed, then all values lie within 0.3–0.7 and the sequence is identical across runs.
- AC-2 [unit] Given diligence 1.0 vs 0.0 with base search duration 60 s and diligence scale 0.5–1.5, then search durations are 90 s and 30 s respectively.
- AC-3 [content] Given a trait outside 0–1, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature with no personality section, when resolved, then all traits default to 0.5 with zero jitter.

items.title: Creature needs (hunger, sleep, fatigue) with behaviour hooks
items.description:
## Why
A hungry beast that can be lured with meat or a guard who dozes at 3am turns creatures into systems the player can read and exploit.

## What
As a thief, I want creatures to eat, sleep and tire so that I can time or engineer my approach. Needs (hunger, sleep, fatigue, plus extensible custom needs) rise over sim time at data-defined rates; satisfiers are world objects tagged with properties (`edible:meat`, `bed`) or schedule windows. Crossing thresholds emits intents (`SeekFood`, `Sleep`) the behaviour runtime may choose. Sleeping creatures use a reduced sense profile.

## Scope
- In: Need decay/satisfaction model
- In: Property-based satisfier discovery via perception
- In: Sleep modifies senses (e.g. sight off, hearing −20 dB)
- Out: Day/night world clock (owned by world/time systems — Related: world clock)
- Out: Poisoned bait (e10 / alchemy post-MVP)

## Notes
Needs must be cheap: update at 1 Hz, not per tick. Related: a world time-of-day clock is needed for schedule windows; if none exists use sim time with a configurable day length.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given hunger rate 10/min and threshold 70, when 7 sim minutes pass from 0, then a `SeekFood` intent is emitted exactly once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a hungry creature that perceives any object tagged `edible:meat` within 15 m, when it chooses `SeekFood`, then its target is the nearest perceived edible object.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a sleeping creature, when a 30 dB noise occurs 5 m away and its awake threshold is 25 dB with sleep penalty 20 dB, then it does not wake; a 50 dB noise wakes it into Suspicious.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an edible object that is removed while a creature walks to it, when it arrives, then the intent fails gracefully and the creature returns to its routine within 3 s.
- AC-5 [unit] Given 200 creatures with needs, when 1 sim hour elapses, then needs update 3,600 times per creature (1 Hz) and never per tick.

items.title: Declare non-hostile creature interactions (feed, talk, calm) in data
items.description:
## Why
Not everything exists solely to be killed. Social creatures (E14) need a framework hook: feeding, talking, intimidating, petting or trading must be declarable per creature.

## What
As a designer, I want to declare which non-hostile verbs a creature accepts and under what conditions so that E14 can build social creatures without new engine code. `interactions`: list of {verb (`talk`, `feed`, `intimidate`, `calm`, `pet`, `trade`, `give`), conditions (disposition range, alert state ∈ {Unaware, Suspicious}, item tag required), outcome event id}. Available verbs surface as contextual prompts via the interaction system; executing emits a typed sim event consumed by dialogue/disposition rules.

## Scope
- In: Schema, condition evaluation, prompt surfacing, outcome events
- In: Alert-state gating (cannot pet a creature in Combat)
- Out: Dialogue trees (e22-dialogue-runtime)
- Out: Specific social creatures and their outcomes (E14)

## Notes
Outcome events feed e12-dispositions modifier rules, e.g. `feed` with any `edible` item applies the `fed` modifier.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P1 — befriending/helping creatures (Brother Horn, the goblins, Clatter) is an MVP constitution pillar and depends on this.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature declaring `feed` requiring item tag `edible:meat`, when the player holds no such item, then the `feed` verb is not offered.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same creature in Combat state, when the player holds meat, then `feed` is not offered.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the grey-box testbed and a fixture creature declaring `feed`, when the player feeds it, then the item is removed from inventory, a `CreatureInteracted{verb: feed}` event fires and disposition rises by the `fed` modifier.
- AC-4 [content] Given an interaction with an unknown verb, when validated, then validation fails listing allowed verbs.
- AC-5 [unit] Given two verbs with overlapping conditions, when prompts are built, then both are offered in declared order.

items.title: Persist creature runtime state across save and load
items.description:
## Why
Failure creates stories only if consequences persist: a guard who is searching, a befriended hound or a knocked-out patrol must survive a reload.

## What
A creature state serializer covering position/facing, health, alert state + timers, memory (last-known positions), morale, needs, disposition, current behaviour node/intent, carried inventory changes (pickpocketed items), and status (`alive`, `unconscious`, `dead`, `befriended`). Integrates with the versioned save format and world state store.

## Scope
- In: Serializer + migration test scaffold
- In: Deterministic resume: a loaded sim continues identically to an unsaved one
- Out: Save UI (E30)
- Out: Global world facts (e27-world-state-store owns them; this item writes creature facts into it)

## Notes
Resume determinism is the key property: save at tick N, load, run to N+M, hash must equal an uninterrupted run.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature in Searching with 12.5 s remaining and an LKP, when saved and loaded, then state, remaining timer and LKP are identical.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a replay of 600 ticks with a save/load at tick 300, when compared with an uninterrupted replay, then sim state hashes at tick 600 are equal.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a save from creature-state schema v1 missing `morale`, when migrated to v2, then morale defaults to 100 and the migration test passes.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unconscious creature, when saved and loaded, then it remains unconscious with its wake timer preserved.

items.title: Auto-generate smoke tests for every creature data file
items.description:
## Why
The test policy requires every creature to have at least one automated test; generating them keeps the bestiary cheap to extend.

## What
A Vitest harness that discovers every `CreatureDef` and runs a standard smoke battery in a headless sim: spawn, tick 10 s, perceive a scripted stimulus (alert state leaves Unaware), execute each declared attack once against a dummy, take lethal damage and die (or respect immunity), despawn. Creature files can opt into extra scenario tests.

## Scope
- In: Discovery, battery, readable per-creature test names
- In: CI integration
- Out: Balance testing (E13 / E34 telemetry)

## Notes
Test names follow `creature:<id> smoke — <step>` so failures point to data.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given N creature files, when the suite runs, then N × (battery size) named tests execute.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a creature whose attack references a missing hitbox, when the suite runs, then only that creature’s attack step fails with the ref name in the message.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a creature immune to all damage types, when the lethal-damage step runs, then the step asserts survival instead of death.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature with no attacks, when the battery runs, then the attack step is skipped and reported as skipped, not passed.

items.title: Write the creature authoring guide with a worked example
items.description:
## Why
The world-content group will author the bestiary in parallel; a single guide keeps creatures consistent and systemic.

## What
A designer guide `docs/content/creatures.md`: every schema section explained, how senses/fears/needs/personality affect AI, property-based vulnerability rules, a worked example built from fixtures (not a real bestiary creature), checklist for a new creature (data, smoke test, placeholder asset ids, prompt bead).

## Scope
- In: Guide + checklist + links to generated schema reference
- Out: Bestiary entries (E13)

## Notes
Link from docs/backlog-contract.md is out of scope for this bead; content group will reference the guide.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the guide, when its worked-example JSON is extracted by a doc test, then it validates against `CreatureDef`.
- AC-2 [manual] Given a designer unfamiliar with the code, when following the checklist, then they can add a new creature that passes the smoke harness in ≤ 30 min.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the generated schema reference, when a schema field is added without documentation, then the doc-coverage check fails.

items.title: Spike: choose AI architecture (utility AI, behaviour trees, HFSM)
items.description:
## Why
Every enemy behaviour sits on this choice. It must be deterministic, data-driven, debuggable and cheap enough for 24+ agents in a browser.

## What
Time-box 2 days. Question: which decision architecture (utility AI, behaviour trees, hierarchical FSM, or hybrid — e.g. HFSM for the 6 alert states with utility selection inside states) best fits deterministic sim, data authoring, debug visualisation and the alert state machine? Build the same scenario (patrol → hear noise → investigate → return) in two candidates inside `spikes/ai-architecture/`, measure tick cost and authoring effort, write an ADR.

## Scope
- In: Two prototype implementations in `spikes/`
- In: Micro-benchmark: 50 agents, cost per tick
- In: ADR `docs/adr/NNNN-ai-architecture.md` with recommendation and data format sketch
- Out: Production runtime (e11-behaviour-runtime)
- Out: Navigation (e11-navigation)

## Notes
Evaluation criteria: determinism (no hidden time/random), data-authorability (JSON), debuggability (current node/scores visualisable), perf, testability at 100% coverage, fit with personality traits and needs as utility inputs.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the spike is complete, when the ADR is reviewed, then it records the decision, at least 2 rejected alternatives with reasons and the measured numbers.
- AC-2 [perf] Given each prototype, when 50 agents run the scenario headless for 60 s, then per-tick cost is recorded (mean and p95) in the ADR.
- AC-3 [unit] Given each prototype, when the scenario replays twice with the same seed, then the agent state hash sequences are identical.
- AC-4 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it includes a JSON sketch of a behaviour definition for `fixture-guard` in the chosen format.

items.title: Implement the deterministic behaviour runtime chosen by the ADR
items.description:
## Why
A single, deterministic behaviour runtime lets all creatures share patrol/investigate/search/combat behaviours authored as data.

## What
Production implementation of the ADR architecture in `src/sim/ai/`: behaviour definitions loaded as content (`behaviour:*`), per-agent blackboard (typed keys), action primitives (move-to, look-at, wait, play-cue, emit-noise, attack), condition primitives (state, stimulus, timer, trait), time-slicing so each agent thinks at a configurable rate (default 10 Hz) with deterministic ordering by entity id.

## Scope
- In: Runtime, primitives, blackboard, behaviour schema + loader
- In: Deterministic scheduler with think budgets
- In: Introspection API for debug visualisation
- Out: Individual behaviours (later E11 items)
- Out: Visual editor (post-MVP, E33)

## Notes
Actions return Running/Success/Failure (or utility equivalents); all timing uses sim ticks. Introspection returns current node/score table per agent.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given two agents with think rate 10 Hz on a 60 Hz sim, when 60 ticks run, then each agent thinks exactly 10 times and their think ticks are staggered deterministically by entity id.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a behaviour definition referencing an unknown primitive, when loaded, then loading fails with the behaviour id and primitive name.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an action that fails (move-to unreachable), when the runtime ticks, then the failure propagates per the ADR semantics and a fallback branch runs.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an agent is despawned mid-action, when the runtime ticks, then no further callbacks run for it and no exception is thrown.
- AC-5 [perf] Given 50 agents running a patrol behaviour, when the sim runs headless, then AI think cost p95 ≤ 1.0 ms per tick on the reference machine.
- AC-6 [unit] Given an agent, when introspected, then it returns the active node path (or top-3 utility scores) as serialisable data.

items.title: Scenario harness for scripted AI tests with asserted states over time
items.description:
## Why
Stealth and AI rules must be trustworthy without reading code; readable, deterministic scenario tests are how we prove guard behaviour.

## What
A test DSL in `src/sim/testing/scenario.ts`: load a grey-box layout (JSON), spawn fixtures with routes, script a player path (waypoints, stance, speed, actions like `throw`, `extinguish`), and assert over time (`at(12.0).expect(guard1).state("Investigating")`, `during(0, 5).expect(guard1).notState("Combat")`). Runs headless on the replay harness; failures print a timeline of state changes and stimuli.

## Scope
- In: DSL, headless runner, failure timeline output
- In: Snapshot hash recording for regression
- In: Example scenario using fixture-guard
- Out: The scenario suite itself (e09-infiltration-scenarios)
- Out: Browser e2e (Playwright)

## Notes
Built on e00-replay-harness; scripted player drives the same input actions as a real player where possible.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a scenario asserting `state("Suspicious")` at t=3.0 s, when the guard is actually Unaware at 3.0 s, then the test fails and output lists every state transition with timestamps.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a scenario, when run twice, then the recorded state hash sequence is identical.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the example scenario (player walks through guard view in light), when run, then the guard transitions Unaware→Suspicious within 1.5 s and the test passes.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a layout JSON referencing an unknown fixture id, when the scenario loads, then it fails before ticking with a clear error.
- AC-5 [perf] Given a 120 s scenario with 6 agents, when run headless in CI, then it completes in ≤ 3 s wall time.

items.title: Navmesh generation and deterministic pathfinding for creatures
items.description:
## Why
Patrol, investigate, search, flee and flank all need reliable paths, including doors, ladders and climb links that make verticality matter.

## What
Navmesh baked from grey-box and level geometry at content build time (Recast-style tool or chosen library, decided within this item), stored as data. Sim-side A* over the navmesh with per-creature capability masks (from e12-locomotion-types), dynamic obstacles (closed/locked doors toggling links), off-mesh links (ladders, jumps, climb). Path smoothing and a request queue with a per-tick budget.

## Scope
- In: Bake step + data format
- In: Pathfinding in sim, deterministic
- In: Door state integration, off-mesh links
- In: Local steering/avoidance between agents (simple)
- Out: Flying 3D navigation beyond height-offset flight (post-MVP)
- Out: Crowd simulation

## Notes
If a WASM library is used, the query layer must still be deterministic and wrapped behind a sim interface with a pure-TS fake for unit tests. Related: level geometry format from E00 greybox kit.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a baked grey-box navmesh, when a path is requested between two connected points, then the returned path is valid (every segment on-mesh) and identical across runs.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a closed locked door between two rooms, when a walker requests a path through it, then no path through that door is returned; after `unlock + open`, the path is found.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a climb link, when a walk-only creature and a climber request the same path, then only the climber’s path uses the link.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unreachable target, when requested, then the result is `Unreachable` with the closest reachable point, not an exception.
- AC-5 [perf] Given 30 path requests in one tick, when the budget is 0.5 ms, then excess requests are deferred to later ticks and all complete within 10 ticks.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the grey-box testbed, when the bake runs, then a navmesh file is produced in ≤ 10 s and content validation passes.

items.title: Creature perception: sight cones, hearing and special senses
items.description:
## Why
Enemies must perceive the world honestly — through senses that the player can understand, predict and exploit — rather than knowing everything.

## What
As a thief, I want enemies to only know what their senses tell them so that darkness, silence and cover genuinely protect me. Each agent evaluates senses from its resolved sense profile: sight (cone test with primary/peripheral zones, vertical limit, range falloff, LOS via e09-line-of-sight, target visibility score via e09-visibility-model, dark-vision factor), hearing (receives noise events from e09-sound-propagation above its threshold), smell/special senses via registered channel handlers. Output is a list of typed stimuli {source, kind, position, strength 0–1, certainty} per think, fed to awareness.

## Scope
- In: Sight, hearing, special-sense channel registry
- In: Stimulus types: seen-target, heard-noise, seen-anomaly, sensed-life
- In: Time-slicing so expensive LOS checks respect a budget
- Out: Awareness accumulation (e11-awareness-accumulation)
- Out: Alert state logic (e11-alert-states)
- Out: Anomaly definitions (e09-anomaly-detection)

## Notes
Perception never reads the player position directly outside senses — enforced by an API boundary (agents receive only stimuli). This is the no-omniscience guarantee.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a guard with primary half-angle 35° and range 20 m, when a fully visible target stands at 10 m and 20° off-axis, then a seen-target stimulus is produced with strength > 0.5.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same target at 10 m and 120° off-axis (outside peripheral), when evaluated, then no sight stimulus is produced.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a target in the cone but with LOS fully blocked, when evaluated, then no sight stimulus is produced.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a target in the cone with visibility score 0.1 (deep shadow, crouched), when evaluated at 15 m, then stimulus strength is below the Suspicious contribution threshold per tuning data.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a noise event of 45 dB at the listener and threshold 30 dB, when evaluated, then a heard-noise stimulus carries the noise’s propagated position, not the true source if the noise was occluded and routed through a doorway.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the perception API, when an agent attempts to access the player entity transform outside a stimulus, then the type system disallows it (compile-time) and an architecture test asserts no such import exists.
- AC-7 [perf] Given 24 agents and 1 target, when perception runs at 10 Hz, then sim perception cost p95 ≤ 0.8 ms per tick on the reference machine.

items.title: Accumulate and decay awareness from stimuli per perceived target
items.description:
## Why
Detection should build gradually so players have time to react; a glimpse at the edge of vision is not the same as walking into a torch-lit room.

## What
Per agent, per perceived source: awareness 0–1 accumulated each think as `strength × senseRate × traitModifiers × dt`, with decay when unstimulated after a grace period. Thresholds from tuning data (e.g. 0.3 Suspicious, 0.6 Investigating, 1.0 Detected) drive alert transitions. Tracks the stimulus that contributed most, used by UI to explain why the player was noticed.

## Scope
- In: Accumulation/decay curves
- In: Per-source records with dominant-cause tracking
- In: Instant-detection rule for very close contact (touch/bump)
- Out: State machine (e11-alert-states)
- Out: UI (e09-awareness-indicators)

## Notes
Curves and thresholds come from e11-ai-tuning-data; this item ships defaults.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a constant sight stimulus of strength 1.0 and rate 1.0/s, when 0.6 s passes, then awareness is 0.6 ± 0.01.
- AC-2 [unit] Given awareness 0.5 and no stimuli, when grace 2 s then decay 0.1/s applies, then awareness is 0.5 at t=2 s and 0.3 at t=4 s.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player bumps into an Unaware guard, when contact is registered, then awareness jumps to 1.0 immediately regardless of light.
- AC-4 [unit] Given sight and hearing stimuli in the same think, when accumulated, then the dominant cause recorded is the one with the larger contribution.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a source that despawns, when the next think runs, then its awareness record is removed without error.

items.title: Six-state alert machine: Unaware to Combat with timed decay
items.description:
## Why
The constitution mandates Unaware → Suspicious → Investigating → Searching → Alerted → Combat. Readable states let players understand and manipulate guards.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to escalate and de-escalate through recognisable states so that I can recover from mistakes. A hierarchical state machine per agent: Unaware, Suspicious (stops, looks toward stimulus), Investigating (moves to stimulus position), Searching (lost the target, searches around last-known position), Alerted (knows an intruder exists, active hunt, may raise alarm), Combat (has a confirmed target in perception). Transitions driven by awareness thresholds, timers and events (ally alarm, damage taken). Each state has a data-defined timeout and fallback. De-escalation goes to a `postAlert` flag (heightened baseline) rather than straight to fully relaxed.

## Scope
- In: States, transition table as data, timers, events emitted on every transition
- In: Damage-from-unseen-source → Alerted (not Combat) since the attacker is unknown
- In: Heightened baseline after de-escalation (faster accumulation)
- Out: Behaviours inside states (investigate/search/combat items)
- Out: Group communication (e11-communication)

## Notes
Transition table example lives in tuning data. Combat → Searching when target lost for > N s; Searching → Unaware(postAlert) after search timeout. Never Combat → Unaware directly.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an Unaware guard, when awareness crosses 0.3, then it enters Suspicious and emits `AlertStateChanged{from: Unaware, to: Suspicious, cause}`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a Suspicious guard, when no stimulus is received for 6 s, then it returns to Unaware with `postAlert=false` and resumes its routine.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a guard in Combat, when the target leaves perception for 5 s, then it enters Searching (never Unaware directly) with the target’s last observed position as LKP.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a Searching guard, when the search timeout (60 s default) elapses without re-acquisition, then it enters Unaware with `postAlert=true` and awareness accumulation rate ×1.5 for 300 s.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an Unaware guard hit by a projectile from an unperceived source, when damage is applied, then it enters Alerted (not Combat) and the LKP is estimated from the projectile direction, not the shooter position.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the transition table, when fuzzed with 10,000 random event sequences, then no transition ever occurs that is absent from the table and state is always one of the six.
- AC-7 [content] Given a tuning file with a timeout ≤ 0, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Target memory and last-known position without omniscience
items.description:
## Why
Enemies must not magically know the player’s position after losing sight. Last-known position is what lets players slip away, double back and set up ambushes.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to hunt where they last saw me, not where I actually am, so that breaking line of sight is meaningful. Agent memory stores per target: LKP, last observed velocity, time last seen, confidence decaying over time, and a bounded prediction (LKP + velocity × min(t, 1.5 s)). Memory updates only from perception stimuli or ally communication. Memories of anomalies (bodies, open doors) persist with timestamps.

## Scope
- In: Memory records, confidence decay, bounded prediction
- In: Update sources: own stimuli, ally reports (tagged second-hand, lower confidence)
- In: Forgetting after configured duration
- Out: Search behaviour choosing where to look (e11-search-behaviour)
- Out: Player-facing LKP ghost (e09-lkp-ghost)

## Notes
Architecture test: memory module has no access to ground-truth transforms. Prediction cap prevents agents tracking the player through walls.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player is last seen at P moving 3 m/s east, when 10 s pass without stimuli, then the predicted position is P + 4.5 m east (capped at 1.5 s) and never updates further.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player, unseen, moves 30 m away, when the guard queries memory, then the returned LKP is unchanged (no leak of true position).
- AC-3 [unit] Given an ally shouts a report of the player at Q, when the listener updates memory, then LKP becomes Q with confidence × 0.7 and source `second-hand`.
- AC-4 [unit] Given confidence decay 0.02/s from 1.0, when 50 s pass, then the memory is forgotten and queries return none.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a scenario where the player breaks LOS around a corner then climbs to a ledge, when the guard arrives at the LKP, then it has no knowledge of the ledge position unless it perceives the player there.

items.title: Patrol routes, guard posts and idle routines authored as data
items.description:
## Why
Believable routines are what a thief observes, times and exploits; they are also where guards return after an alert.

## What
As a designer, I want to author patrol routes and posts in level data so that guards have readable, exploitable routines. Route types: loop, ping-pong, random-weighted graph; waypoints with dwell time, look-direction, and optional idle action (lean, warm hands at fire, check door). Posts: stationary with scan arcs. Routines can be scheduled by time windows. Agents remember their routine and resume the nearest sensible waypoint after an alert.

## Scope
- In: Route/post schema in level data, runtime behaviour
- In: Idle action hooks as cue ids
- In: Resume-nearest-waypoint logic
- Out: Day/night schedules beyond simple windows (Related: world clock)
- Out: Animation assets (placeholder cues only)

## Notes
Random-weighted routes use seeded RNG per agent.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a loop route A→B→C with 2 s dwell at each, when simulated, then the guard visits A, B, C, A in order with dwell ±1 tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a ping-pong route, when the guard reaches the last waypoint, then it reverses direction.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a guard returning from Searching, when it resumes, then it paths to the nearest waypoint on its route by nav distance, not the next index.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a route waypoint that becomes unreachable (door locked), when the guard attempts it, then it skips to the next reachable waypoint and emits a `RouteBlocked` event (door-check anomaly hook).
- AC-5 [content] Given a route referencing a nonexistent waypoint id, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Guards investigate suspicious stimuli at their perceived location
items.description:
## Why
Distractions only work if guards go and look. Investigation is the core lever for thrown objects, noises and glimpses.

## What
As a thief, I want a guard to walk over and check a noise or glimpse so that I can lure him away from his post. In Suspicious: stop, turn toward stimulus, text bark cue. In Investigating: path to stimulus position at walk (or cautious) gait, look around on arrival with a scan pattern, inspect the source object if perceived (e.g. a thrown bottle), then decide: nothing found → de-escalate; more stimuli → escalate. Multiple stimuli: most recent strong one wins; weaker stimuli queue up to 3.

## Scope
- In: Investigate behaviour, scan pattern, source inspection, stimulus queue
- In: Cautious gait when postAlert
- Out: Group investigation roles (e11-communication)
- Out: Search around LKP (e11-search-behaviour)

## Notes
Investigation position is the perceived position (may be offset by sound routing), not the true source.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an Investigating guard with target position 12 m away, when simulated, then it arrives within (12 / walkSpeed + 1) s and performs a scan of ≥ 3 look directions.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a second, louder stimulus while investigating, when perceived, then the guard retargets to the new position and the first is queued.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an unreachable stimulus position (on a roof), when investigating, then the guard moves to the closest reachable point, looks toward the position for the scan duration, then de-escalates.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a scenario where a noise occurs behind a closed door, when the guard investigates, then it opens the door (if unlocked) before scanning the room.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a queue already holding 3 stimuli, when a 4th weaker stimulus arrives, then the weakest is dropped.

items.title: Search patterns around last-known position, including hiding spots
items.description:
## Why
A convincing search — fanning out, checking corners and wardrobes — makes escaping feel earned, and gives up plausibly so failure does not force a reload.

## What
As a thief, I want searching guards to check plausible places near where they lost me so that hiding well matters and hiding badly gets me caught. Searching generates candidate points around LKP (+ bounded prediction): nav-reachable points ranked by distance, cover/darkness, and whether the point is out of sight from LKP; plus hiding spots within radius. Agents claim points (no two agents search the same point), check hiding spots with a probability based on whether they saw the target enter it, expand radius over time, then give up.

## Scope
- In: Candidate generation, ranking, claiming, radius expansion
- In: Hiding-spot checks with probability rules
- In: Diligence trait scaling of duration
- Out: Hiding place mechanics (e09-hiding-places)
- Out: Alarm raising (e11-communication)

## Notes
Probability of checking a hiding spot: 1.0 if target was seen entering; otherwise base 0.25 scaled by proximity to LKP. Seeded RNG.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a Searching guard with LKP L, when candidates are generated, then all lie within the current radius, are nav-reachable and the first 3 are sorted by the ranking function.
- AC-2 [unit] Given two guards searching the same LKP, when they claim points, then no point is claimed by both.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the guard saw the target enter a hiding spot, when searching, then it checks that spot first with probability 1.0.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a hiding spot not seen being entered, 10 m from LKP, when evaluated with a fixed seed, then the check decision matches the documented probability formula.
- AC-5 [unit] Given no reachable candidates (LKP on an isolated ledge), when searching, then the guard looks toward LKP from the nearest point, then de-escalates at the search timeout without error.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a scenario where the player hides in darkness 8 m from LKP and stays still, when a single guard searches for 60 s, then the guard ends Searching without entering Combat in the scripted seed.

items.title: Allies share alerts by shouts, sight signals and alarm devices
items.description:
## Why
Enemies that communicate make a single mistake escalate believably, and give players targets — silence the shouter, cut the bell rope.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to call for help through the world rather than telepathy so that I can prevent or exploit alarms. Channels: shout (emits a loud noise event via sound propagation carrying a report: LKP, state), visual signal (allies in LOS within 25 m receive the report), alarm device (agents path to a nearest `alarm` object and activate it via the interaction/mechanism system, broadcasting Alerted to a faction zone). Only allies (faction relation ally/friendly) accept reports. Group roles in Alerted/Searching: one caller, others flank/search.

## Scope
- In: Report message type, shout/visual/alarm channels
- In: Faction filtering
- In: Basic role assignment (caller, searcher, guard-post-holder)
- Out: Reinforcement spawning (e09-failed-stealth-outcomes)
- Out: Speech/voice (text barks only — e09-alert-barks)

## Notes
Alarm objects are world mechanisms with an `alarm` property; if destroyed or jammed, the AI must fall back to shouting. Related: alarm bell mechanism may be authored with E03 switches.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a guard entering Alerted, when it shouts, then a noise event of the configured loudness is emitted and allies whose perceived level exceeds their hearing threshold receive the report.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a guard behind 2 closed doors whose shout is attenuated below an ally’s threshold, when shouting, then that ally receives nothing.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature of a hostile faction within hearing, when a shout occurs, then it does not receive the report (it may still perceive the noise as a stimulus).
- AC-4 [unit] Given an alarm object that has been disabled (jammed or destroyed), when a guard attempts to use it, then it falls back to shouting within 2 s.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a scenario with 3 guards and one alarm bell, when the first guard spots the player and reaches the bell, then all guards in the bell’s zone enter Alerted within 1 tick of activation.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a guard is knocked out mid-path to the alarm, when the tick runs, then no alarm activation occurs.

items.title: Combat behaviour: engage, space, select attacks and share targets
items.description:
## Why
Combat is intrinsically fun only if enemies fight readably: spacing, telegraphing, taking turns and punishing mistakes.

## What
As a knight, I want enemies to circle, pressure and take turns so that fights reward reading behaviour. In Combat: maintain preferred range per creature, strafe/circle, pick attacks from `attacks` by preconditions + weights + personality aggression, respect an attack token budget per target (max N simultaneous attackers, default 2), react to player block/parry (stagger response), reposition when target is out of reach (path/wait/ranged fallback).

## Scope
- In: Engage/space/attack-select loop
- In: Attack token manager
- In: Out-of-reach handling (e.g. player on ledge)
- Out: Retreat/flee (e11-retreat-flee)
- Out: Boss-specific patterns (E13/E26)

## Notes
All selection deterministic with seeded RNG. Losing the target transitions via alert states to Searching.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 4 hostile guards in Combat vs one player with token budget 2, when simulated for 10 s, then at no tick are more than 2 guards in an attack windup/active phase.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an attack whose precondition (distance ≤ 2 m) is false, when selecting, then it is never chosen.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player stands on a ledge unreachable by nav, when a melee-only guard is in Combat, then it moves to the closest point, waits and after 8 s transitions to a taunt/wait behaviour rather than jittering (≤ 1 path request per second).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the grey-box fight room, when the player fights 2 fixture guards, then both guards attack at least once within 10 s and the fight resolves without AI errors.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a guard is staggered, when the stagger ends, then it re-evaluates attack selection rather than resuming the cancelled attack.

items.title: Creatures retreat, flee to allies and cower based on morale
items.description:
## Why
Enemies that retreat, regroup or flee make fights and scares feel alive and allow non-lethal victories.

## What
As a player, I want frightened or wounded creatures to disengage so that encounters end in more ways than death. Consumes `Flee`/`Cower` intents from e12-fears-morale and health thresholds: flee away from the fear source toward allies, safe zones or a lair point; cower when cornered; regroup and re-enter Alerted/Searching when morale recovers. Fleeing creatures may shout (communication) and drop carried items (hook).

## Scope
- In: Flee destination scoring, cower, regroup
- In: Surrender intent event (hook for E14 dialogue)
- Out: Morale model (e12-fears-morale)
- Out: Surrender dialogue (E14/E22)

## Notes
Flee destination scoring: distance from threat, ally proximity, darkness preference per creature.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with a `Flee` intent and threat at T, when fleeing, then after 3 s its distance from T has increased and its path does not pass within 2 m of T.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fleeing creature with no escape path (dead end), when cornered, then it enters `Cower` within 1 s.
- AC-3 [unit] Given morale recovers above the regroup threshold, when the intent clears, then the creature enters Searching with the threat’s last-known position.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature tagged `fearless` (morale disabled), when at 1 health, then it never flees.

items.title: Guards return to routines, visibly changed by what happened
items.description:
## Why
Failure creates stories: after an alert guards should go back to work, but the world should remember — lit torches, doubled posts, grumbling barks.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to settle back down after an alert but stay changed so that my mistakes reshape the level instead of resetting it. On de-escalation: path back to routine, apply post-alert adjustments from data (e.g. relight extinguished lights on route, close opened doors, patrol in pairs, add a checkpoint post, carry a torch), keep heightened awareness for a duration. Adjustments are data-driven per behaviour profile and recorded as world facts.

## Scope
- In: Return behaviour, post-alert adjustment list, persistence via world state
- In: Barks cue on return
- Out: Level lockdowns/reinforcements (e09-failed-stealth-outcomes)

## Notes
Adjustments list example: `relight-seen-extinguished-lights`, `close-seen-open-doors`, `pair-up`, `carry-torch`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a guard de-escalates with `postAlert=true`, when simulated, then it resumes its route within 5 s and awareness rate multiplier is 1.5 for 300 s, then 1.0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a guard with the `relight-seen-extinguished-lights` adjustment that perceived an extinguished torch during the alert, when returning, then it paths to the torch and relights it before resuming.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the torch was destroyed (not merely extinguished), when the adjustment runs, then the guard skips it and switches to `carry-torch` if declared.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a save after an alert with `pair-up` applied, when loaded, then the paired patrol persists.

items.title: Author AI tuning data: thresholds, decay timers, search durations
items.description:
## Why
Stealth feel is tuned constantly; all numbers must be data so designers can iterate without code and tests can pin defaults.

## What
A `AiTuning` schema and default files per behaviour profile: awareness thresholds per state, accumulation rates per sense, grace and decay timers, state timeouts (Suspicious 6 s, Investigating 20 s, Searching 60 s, Alerted 120 s defaults), post-alert multiplier and duration, search radius growth, token budgets, think rates. Profiles inherit (`guard-default` → `guard-lazy`). Hot-reload in dev.

## Scope
- In: Schema, inheritance, defaults, hot reload in dev builds
- In: Pinned default-value tests
- Out: Sense ranges (e12-sense-profiles)
- Out: Stealth emitter tuning (e09-stealth-tuning-data)

## Notes
Changing defaults requires updating pinned tests deliberately — that is the point.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the default tuning files, when validated, then every state has a positive timeout and thresholds are strictly increasing Suspicious < Investigating < Detected.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `guard-lazy` inheriting from `guard-default` overriding only Searching timeout 30 s, when resolved, then all other values equal the parent.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an inheritance cycle, when loaded, then loading fails naming the cycle.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a dev build, when a tuning file is edited, then running agents use the new values within 1 s without reload.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the shipped defaults, when the pinned-default test runs, then each documented default matches.

items.title: AI debug overlay: sight cones, hearing, states, LKP and paths
items.description:
## Why
AI is untuneable if you cannot see what it thinks. Developers need to see every agent’s senses, state and memory live.

## What
As a developer, I want a toggleable AI overlay so that I can understand and tune behaviour in seconds. Per agent: sight cone (primary/peripheral, tinted by alert state), hearing radius, awareness bars per source, state label + time in state, active behaviour node / top utility scores, LKP marker with confidence, current path, claimed search points. Global: noise event rings with loudness and propagation route, light level probe under cursor. Console: `ai.debug on|off|select <id>`, `ai.freeze`, `ai.step`.

## Scope
- In: Overlay rendering from sim introspection data
- In: Console commands incl. freeze/step
- In: Selection by clicking an agent
- Out: Player-facing stealth UI (E09 UI items)
- Out: Visual behaviour editor (post-MVP)

## Notes
Render layer reads introspection snapshots; sim must not depend on overlay. Overlay code excluded from unit coverage per coverage-exclusions.md; introspection data builders are 100% covered in sim.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an agent, when the introspection snapshot is built, then it contains state, timeInState, awareness per source, LKP, path and cone parameters.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the grey-box testbed with 3 guards, when `ai.debug on` is entered, then overlay elements for 3 agents render with no console errors.
- AC-3 [integration] Given `ai.freeze`, when 60 frames render, then the sim tick counter does not advance; `ai.step` advances exactly 1 tick.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the overlay on with 24 agents, when measured, then added frame time p95 ≤ 2 ms on the reference machine (High).
- AC-5 [unit] Given the overlay is off, when the sim runs, then no introspection snapshots are built (zero overhead check via counter).

items.title: Perf budget: 24 active AI agents within sim frame budget
items.description:
## Why
The hardware baseline requires steady 60 fps; AI perception, pathing and sound propagation are the likeliest sim hot spots.

## What
Add an AI stress scene and budget tests: 24 agents (mixed fixtures) in Alerted/Searching with continuous noise events and a moving target. Budgets: total AI+perception+sound sim cost p95 ≤ 3 ms per tick on the reference machine; ≤ 5 ms on the Low-preset class machine. Includes LOS cache and level-of-detail think rates (agents > 40 m from player think at 2 Hz).

## Scope
- In: Stress scene, budget assertions, AI LOD think rates, LOS result caching
- Out: Render perf (E32)

## Notes
Numbers cite the contract hardware baseline.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the AI stress scene with 24 agents, when run for 60 s headless on the reference machine, then AI+perception+sound cost p95 ≤ 3 ms per tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an agent 50 m from the player with LOD enabled, when 60 ticks run, then it thinks 2 times; within 40 m it thinks 10 times.
- AC-3 [unit] Given AI LOD, when an out-of-range agent receives a noise stimulus above threshold, then it is promoted to full think rate on the next tick (no missed alerts).
- AC-4 [perf] Given the stress scene in the browser (High), when measured, then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms.

items.title: Multi-point line-of-sight queries with partial cover and see-through
items.description:
## Why
Hiding behind a crate with your head poking out should be different from full cover; windows and grates should let guards see but not pass.

## What
A sim LOS service: raycast from the observer’s eye to N sample points on the target (head, chest, hips, feet — configurable) returning fraction visible 0–1. Colliders carry an `occlusion` property: `opaque`, `transparent` (glass, grates), `partial:<factor>` (foliage, curtains, smoke volumes). Queries go through a physics adapter with a pure-TS fake for unit tests.

## Scope
- In: LOS service, sample points, occlusion properties, adapter + fake
- In: Dynamic occluders (smoke volumes, closing doors)
- Out: Visibility score composition (e09-visibility-model)
- Out: Sight cone logic (e11-perception)

## Notes
Smoke and foliage are volumes; their factor multiplies along the ray. Batch API for many observers per tick.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a target fully behind an `opaque` wall, when queried, then visible fraction is 0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a target crouched behind a crate that hides hips and feet only, when queried with 4 sample points, then visible fraction is 0.5.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a target behind a `transparent` window, when queried, then visible fraction equals the unobstructed value.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a ray through two `partial:0.5` foliage volumes, when queried, then the per-ray visibility is 0.25.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a zero-length ray (observer eye inside target), when queried, then visible fraction is 1 and no error is thrown.
- AC-6 [perf] Given 24 observers × 4 samples, when batched, then the query cost p95 ≤ 0.3 ms per tick on the reference machine.

items.title: Compute player visibility from light, stance, motion and distance
items.description:
## Why
Stealth cannot be crouching plus an eye icon. Visibility must emerge from light and darkness, stance, movement and distance so players can reason about it.

## What
As a thief, I want how visible I am to depend on the light on my body, my stance, how fast I move and what I wear so that shadows and patience are my tools. `visibility(target, observer)` = lightTerm (light-field sample at target sample points, adjusted by observer dark-vision) × stanceTerm (prone/crouch/stand) × motionTerm (speed band) × profileTerm (equipment brightness, disguise/cloak modifiers) × LOS fraction × distance falloff. A per-target self-visibility (observer-independent) is also exposed for the HUD.

## Scope
- In: Pure function + components, all weights from tuning data
- In: Self-visibility for UI
- In: Contrast rule: a silhouette against a bright background raises visibility
- Out: Sight cone / accumulation (E11)
- Out: Light-field implementation (e03-light-field)

## Notes
Terms multiply so any zero term hides the target. Keep the function pure: inputs are sampled values, not entity lookups, for trivial unit testing.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given light level 0.05 at all sample points, crouched and still at 10 m, when computed with default tuning, then visibility ≤ 0.1.
- AC-2 [unit] Given light level 0.9, standing and sprinting at 10 m, when computed, then visibility ≥ 0.8.
- AC-3 [unit] Given identical inputs except distance 5 m vs 20 m, when computed, then the 20 m result is strictly lower per the falloff curve.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an observer with dark-vision 1.0, when the target stands in 0.0 light, then the light term is 1.0 (darkness gives no benefit).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a dark target silhouetted against a background light ≥ 0.7 along the observer ray, when computed, then the contrast bonus applies and visibility rises by the configured amount.
- AC-6 [unit] Given LOS fraction 0, when computed, then visibility is exactly 0 regardless of other terms.
- AC-7 [content] Given the stealth tuning file, when a weight is outside 0–2, then validation fails.

items.title: Propagate noise events through rooms, doors and walls with occlusion
items.description:
## Why
Sound propagation, surfaces and doors are constitution-mandated stealth inputs. Guards should hear a dropped bottle through an open door but not through thick stone.

## What
As a thief, I want noise to travel like it does in a building so that closing a door or taking the long way round actually keeps me quiet. Noise events {source, loudness dB at 1 m, kind, tags} propagate over a room/portal graph built from level data: distance attenuation (inverse-square approximation in dB), portal attenuation by door state (open 0 dB, ajar −6 dB, closed −20 dB, configurable per door material), wall transmission for adjacent rooms (−30 dB default, per wall material), floor/ceiling transmission for verticality. Listeners receive perceived level and the perceived position (the last portal the sound came through when routed indirectly).

## Scope
- In: Room/portal graph build from level data
- In: Propagation (Dijkstra over portals, bounded)
- In: Perceived position routing
- In: Event bus API for emitters (footsteps, impacts, shouts, spells)
- In: Hook for e28-audio-engine to reuse the occlusion result
- Out: Footstep emission rules (e09-footstep-noise)
- Out: Actual audio playback (e28-audio-engine)

## Notes
Perceived position is what makes the no-omniscience rule hold for sound. Bounded search: stop when level < global floor (10 dB).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 60 dB noise and a listener 10 m away in the same room, when propagated, then perceived level is 40 dB ± 0.5 (−20 dB for 10 m).
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same geometry with a closed door on the only path, when propagated, then perceived level is 20 dB lower than with the door open.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a noise in room A heard in room B via a doorway, when propagated, then the perceived position is the doorway, not the source.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two paths (open corridor 25 m, closed door 8 m), when propagated, then the louder of the two routes is used.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a noise on the floor above through a wooden floor (−15 dB), when propagated to a listener below, then perceived level reflects the floor transmission loss.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a door that changes from open to closed between two noise events, when the second event propagates, then it uses the new door state (graph edges update on door events).
- AC-7 [unit] Given a noise emitted outside any room (open terrain), when propagated, then pure distance attenuation applies without error.
- AC-8 [perf] Given 20 noise events per tick in a 60-room level, when propagated, then cost p95 ≤ 0.5 ms per tick.

items.title: Tag surfaces with acoustic materials that change footstep noise
items.description:
## Why
Surfaces are a constitution stealth input: carpet muffles, gravel crunches, a creaky board betrays you, a puddle splashes.

## What
Acoustic material tags on walkable colliders and level regions (`stone`, `wood`, `wood-creaky`, `carpet`, `gravel`, `metal-grate`, `water-shallow`, `grass`, `leaves`, `glass-shards`): loudness offset dB, per-step variance, and sfx set id. Materials can change dynamically via world properties (a `wet` or `frozen` surface changes its offset; scattered glass shards become `glass-shards`). Query API `surfaceAt(position)`.

## Scope
- In: Material table (content data), collider/region tagging, dynamic modifiers from world properties
- In: Grey-box painter support: tag via level JSON
- Out: Footstep emission rule (e09-footstep-noise)
- Out: Final footstep audio (asset beads)

## Notes
Creaky boards: probability per step of an extra +12 dB creak (seeded).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a position on a `carpet` region, when `surfaceAt` is queried, then material is `carpet` with offset −10 dB (default table).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a `wood` surface that gains the `frozen` property, when queried, then the frozen-surface modifier applies per the table.
- AC-3 [unit] Given overlapping regions, when queried, then the higher-priority region wins deterministically.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a position with no surface tag, when queried, then the default `stone` material is returned and a dev warning is logged once per region.
- AC-5 [content] Given the material table, when validated, then each material has an offset in −20..+20 dB and a sfx set id.

items.title: Emit footstep noise from speed, stance, surface and equipment weight
items.description:
## Why
Silent movement must be a skill: running on gravel in plate armour should wake the keep; creeping barefoot over carpet should not.

## What
As a thief, I want my footsteps to be as loud as my choices make them so that moving slowly and choosing my path pays off. Each footstep (from controller gait cadence) emits a noise event: base dB by gait (sneak/walk/run/sprint) + surface offset + equipment noise (sum of equipped item `noise` values, e.g. plate clank) + landing impulse for jumps/falls (by fall height). Also emitted for any creature with footsteps, so the player can hear guards.

## Scope
- In: Footstep emission rule shared by player and creatures
- In: Landing and falling impacts
- In: Equipment noise aggregation (reads item data)
- Out: Progression perks that reduce noise (e10-silent-movement)
- Out: Audio playback (e28)

## Notes
Emit at step cadence, not per tick. Defaults: sneak 25, walk 40, run 55, sprint 65 dB at 1 m.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player sneaking on carpet with no noisy equipment, when a step occurs, then the event loudness is 15 dB (25 − 10).
- AC-2 [unit] Given sprinting on gravel wearing items with total noise +10 dB, when a step occurs, then loudness is 65 + gravel offset + 10.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a fall of 3 m onto stone, when landing, then an impact event with loudness per the fall-height curve is emitted once.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player standing still, when 5 s pass, then no footstep events are emitted.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a scenario where the player sneaks past a guard 6 m away on carpet, when simulated, then the guard stays Unaware; the same path sprinting on gravel makes the guard Suspicious within 1 s.

items.title: Author stealth tuning data: light weights, stance, noise, doors
items.description:
## Why
Stealth feel must be tunable by designers without code, and defaults pinned by tests.

## What
