A `StealthTuning` schema and default file: light-term curve, stance multipliers, motion bands, distance falloff, contrast bonus, gait base dB, surface table link, door-state and wall/floor transmission defaults, global audibility floor, hiding-place concealment defaults. Hot reload in dev; difficulty presets can override a whitelisted subset.

## Scope
- In: Schema, defaults, hot reload, pinned default tests
- In: Difficulty override whitelist (consumed by e09-stealth-assists)
- Out: AI thresholds and timers (e11-ai-tuning-data)
- Out: Sense ranges (e12-sense-profiles)

## Notes
Curves are piecewise-linear point lists for easy editing.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the default file, when validated, then all curves are monotonic in the documented direction.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a difficulty preset overriding a non-whitelisted key, when loaded, then loading fails naming the key.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a dev build, when the stance multiplier is edited, then the visibility HUD reflects the change within 1 s.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the shipped defaults, when the pinned-default test runs, then documented values match.

items.title: Verticality rules: limited upward vision and height advantage
items.description:
## Why
Verticality is a stealth input: rafters, balconies and rooftops should be real thief highways because guards rarely look up.

## What
As a thief, I want to be harder to notice above or below a guard’s eye line so that rafters and ledges become routes. Vertical sight: per-profile vertical half-angles up/down (humanoids look up poorly by default, e.g. +20° up, −45° down) with an extra falloff; creatures with `looks-up` tag (e.g. spiders, fliers) ignore it; Searching agents perform occasional look-up scans. Height difference affects noise via floor transmission (already in propagation) and adds a visibility penalty when the target is above a lit area but itself in dark rafters.

## Scope
- In: Vertical cone limits + falloff
- In: Look-up scan in Searching/Investigating when LKP is elevated
- In: Tuning data
- Out: Climbing movement (e10-climbing)
- Out: Flying creature navigation (post-MVP)

## Notes
LKP elevation > 2 m above agent eye triggers look-up scan behaviour.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a humanoid guard with vertical up half-angle 20°, when the target is 30° above horizontal at 8 m, then no sight stimulus is produced while the guard is Unaware.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature tagged `looks-up`, when the same target is evaluated, then a sight stimulus is produced.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a Searching guard whose LKP is 4 m above its eye height, when it reaches the LKP area, then it performs a look-up scan that widens its up half-angle to 60° for 3 s.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a scenario where the player crosses rafters above 2 patrolling guards in a lit hall, when simulated, then neither guard exceeds Suspicious.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the target directly overhead (90°), when evaluated, then no division-by-zero or NaN occurs and visibility follows the vertical rule.

items.title: Hiding places: wardrobes, barrels, tall grass and shadowed alcoves
items.description:
## Why
Hiding places are a constitution stealth input and give failed stealth a recovery move rather than a reload.

## What
As a thief, I want to duck into a wardrobe, crouch in tall grass or press into an alcove so that I can break pursuit if I am quick and unseen. Two kinds: enter-able containers (wardrobe, barrel, under-bed — interact to enter/exit, player hidden, limited view) and concealment volumes (tall grass, curtains, alcoves — visibility multiplier while inside and stationary/crouched). Data: concealment factor, entry noise dB, entry time, capacity, `searchable` flag. AI that saw you enter knows; AI searching may check (e11-search-behaviour). Being found inside = instant Combat at close range with a brief stagger window to flee (failure creates a story).

## Scope
- In: Hiding place component + data
- In: Enter/exit via interaction with timing and noise
- In: Concealment volumes feeding visibility model
- In: Being-discovered outcome
- Out: Hiding bodies in containers (e10-body-carry-hide)
- Out: Hiding prop art (placeholder boxes)

## Notes
Entering while observed must be tracked as a memory `saw-enter:<hidingPlaceId>`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player inside a wardrobe, when any observer computes visibility, then the result is 0 unless the wardrobe is opened by that observer.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player crouched still in tall grass (concealment 0.3), when visibility is computed, then it is multiplied by 0.3; moving at run speed removes the bonus.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a guard observes the player entering a barrel, when the guard searches, then the barrel is checked first (via memory `saw-enter`).
- AC-4 [unit] Given an occupied single-capacity hiding place, when a second entity attempts to enter, then entry is refused with a prompt reason.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a guard opens the wardrobe the player is in, when discovered, then the guard enters Combat and the player gets a 0.6 s stagger window during which exiting is possible.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when the player enters and exits a wardrobe via the interact action, then the camera switches to the hiding view and back without errors.

items.title: Guards notice world anomalies: bodies, open doors, dark torches
items.description:
## Why
A thief’s actions leave traces; guards noticing a doused torch or a missing colleague creates tension and new situations.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to notice what I changed so that covering my tracks is part of the craft. Anomalies are world facts compared against an agent’s expected state (routine knowledge): unconscious/dead bodies, doors open that are normally closed, lights extinguished that are normally lit, missing valuables from a watched spot, blood/broken objects, a colleague missing from post for > N s. Each anomaly type has data: detection via sight (uses visibility of the anomaly), suspicion weight, resulting state (Suspicious for an open door, Alerted for a body).

## Scope
- In: Anomaly registry + expected-state baseline per area/agent
- In: Perception integration (seen-anomaly stimulus)
- In: Data-driven anomaly types + weights
- Out: Relighting/closing on return (e11-return-to-routine)
- Out: Body carrying (e10-body-carry-hide)

## Notes
Expected state captured at level load and updated when guards themselves change things. Hidden bodies (in containers or darkness below visibility threshold) are not perceived.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a door normally closed is open, when a guard perceives it, then it becomes Suspicious and investigates the door.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a guard perceives an unconscious body, when evaluated, then it enters Alerted, investigates the body and may wake it (unconscious ally wakes after 3 s interaction).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a body placed in a container or in light ≤ 0.1 beyond 6 m, when a guard walks its route, then the body is not perceived.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a torch normally lit is extinguished, when a guard perceives the dark torch, then it becomes Suspicious (not Alerted) with cause `light-out`.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a guard itself opened a door on its route, when it later perceives that door open, then no anomaly is raised.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a scenario where the player knocks out guard A and leaves the body in a lit corridor on guard B’s route, when guard B passes, then guard B enters Alerted within 2 s of the body entering its view.

items.title: Stealth HUD: light exposure, noise ring and stance readout
items.description:
## Why
Stealth cannot be an eye icon: the player needs to read the inputs — how lit they are and how loud they are — to make decisions.

## What
As a thief, I want to see how exposed and how loud I am so that I can make informed choices. Elements: light-exposure gem (continuous, 5 visual bands, driven by self-visibility), noise ring around the character footprint that pulses at each emitted noise scaled to its audible radius for a typical guard, stance/gait indicator, and optional diegetic cue (character material darkens in shadow). All toggleable and scalable via settings.

## Scope
- In: HUD components in `src/ui`, data binding from sim
- In: Placeholder art (CSS/SVG shapes)
- In: Settings toggles
- Out: Per-enemy awareness (e09-awareness-indicators)
- Out: Final UI art (asset beads)

## Notes
Noise ring radius = distance at which the emitted noise drops to the baseline humanoid hearing threshold in open space.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given self-visibility 0.05, when the HUD model is computed, then the gem shows band 1 of 5; at 0.95 band 5.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a 40 dB footstep and a 30 dB baseline threshold, when the noise ring is computed, then its radius is ≈ 3.2 m (10^(10/20)).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the settings toggle `hud.stealth=false`, when the HUD renders, then no stealth elements are present.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when the player walks from a lit area into shadow, then the gem band decreases within 250 ms.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a playtest with 3 players, when asked to explain the gem and ring without instructions after 5 min, then at least 2 describe both correctly.

items.title: Directional awareness indicators showing each enemy’s alert state
items.description:
## Why
Players must see who is noticing them, from where, how close to detection, and why — without the omniscient radar that kills tension.

## What
As a thief, I want directional indicators for enemies becoming aware of me so that I can react before being caught. For each agent with awareness > 0 of the player: an indicator near the agent (on-screen) or screen-edge chevron (off-screen) that fills with awareness and changes shape per alert state (6 distinct shapes, not colour alone), plus a cause glyph (eye = saw, ear = heard, hand = anomaly). Indicators only appear for agents the player could plausibly perceive (on-screen or heard), preserving uncertainty.

## Scope
- In: Indicator model from awareness + state + dominant cause
- In: On-screen and off-screen rendering
- In: Colour-blind-safe shapes
- Out: Text barks (e09-alert-barks)
- Out: Last-known-position ghost (e09-lkp-ghost)

## Notes
Indicators for agents the player has not perceived (behind walls, silent) are hidden unless an accessibility assist enables them (e09-stealth-assists).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an agent at awareness 0.45 in Suspicious caused by hearing, when the indicator model is built, then fill = 0.45, shape = `suspicious`, glyph = `ear`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an agent behind a wall that has not been seen or heard by the player, when the model is built with assists off, then no indicator is produced.
- AC-3 [unit] Given each of the six states, when shapes are resolved, then six distinct shape ids are returned.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when a guard off-screen to the left becomes Suspicious from a noise, then a left-edge chevron appears within 1 frame of the state change.
- AC-5 [unit] Given 12 aware agents, when the model is built, then at most 6 indicators are shown, prioritised by awareness × proximity.

items.title: Show a last-known-position ghost where enemies think you are
items.description:
## Why
Showing where guards believe you are turns last-known position into a tool — the player can see the gap between belief and reality and exploit it.

## What
As a thief, I want to see a faint silhouette where the enemies last saw me so that I can plan to double back or set up an ambush. When at least one hunting agent (Searching/Alerted) holds a player LKP and the player is out of its perception, render a translucent silhouette at the LKP in the stance last observed. Disappears when all agents lose the memory or re-acquire. Toggleable.

## Scope
- In: Ghost model from aggregated agent memories
- In: Placeholder translucent capsule silhouette
- In: Settings toggle
- Out: Accurate player mesh silhouette (asset integration later)

## Notes
Aggregate: show the most recent LKP among hunting agents; if two diverge by > 10 m, show both.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given one Searching agent with an LKP and no perception of the player, when the ghost model is built, then one ghost at that LKP is returned.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the agent re-acquires the player, when the model is built, then no ghost is returned.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two hunting agents with LKPs 15 m apart, when built, then two ghosts are returned; if 5 m apart, one.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when the player breaks LOS from an Alerted guard, then a ghost appears at the break point within 250 ms.

items.title: Text barks and audio stingers on alert state transitions
items.description:
## Why
Players read enemy minds through barks ("Who’s there?", "Must be rats…"). With no voice in MVP, text barks plus audio stingers carry this.

## What
As a thief, I want guards to mutter and call out as their state changes so that I understand what they think without a UI meter. Bark tables per behaviour profile map (transition, cause) → weighted lines, shown as floating subtitle text near the speaker within hearing range; audio stinger per escalation (placeholder tones) via the audio engine; cooldowns prevent spam. Barks also enable stealth-layer music hooks.

## Scope
- In: Bark table schema + selection (seeded)
- In: Floating text renderer with distance fade
- In: Stinger cue ids + cooldowns
- Out: Voice acting (no voice in MVP)
- Out: Adaptive music system (Related: E28/E38 music layering)
- Out: Final bark writing (narrative pass, Related: e39-story-bible tone)

## Notes
Stingers: `sfx-stealth-suspicious-01`, `sfx-stealth-alerted-01`, `sfx-stealth-combat-01`, `sfx-stealth-lost-01` — placeholder beeps until asset beads land.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a Unaware→Suspicious transition with cause `heard`, when a bark is selected with a fixed seed, then it comes from the `suspicious.heard` table and is deterministic.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same agent barked 2 s ago with cooldown 5 s, when a new transition occurs, then no bark is shown.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a speaker 40 m away beyond hearing range, when a bark would show, then it is suppressed for the player.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an escalation to Alerted, when it occurs, then exactly one stinger cue is played via the audio engine.
- AC-5 [content] Given a bark table referencing an unknown transition key, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Failed stealth escalates into new situations, not reload screens
items.description:
## Why
Failure creates stories. Being spotted should cause lockdowns, reinforcements, changed patrols or a chase — situations the player can still play through.

## What
As a thief, I want getting caught to change the level rather than end my run so that I can improvise an escape. Area alarm levels (0 calm, 1 wary, 2 alarm, 3 lockdown) per zone driven by alarms, bodies found and combat. Data-defined responses per zone and level: lock specified doors, light extra lights, reinforce posts from a reserve pool (pre-placed, activated — not spawned from nowhere), release hounds, shift patrols; decay back after N minutes of calm to a stable “wary” level, never fully reset. Responses recorded in world state.

## Scope
- In: Zone alarm model + response data + decay
- In: Integration with doors, lights, reserve creatures
- In: World state persistence
- Out: Crime/bounty system across settlements (Related: E22/E27 crime; not in this epic)
- Out: Specific dungeon zone authoring (E26)

## Notes
Reserve pool creatures are placed in level data with `reserve: <zone>`; activation paths them in from their barracks so the player can see them come.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given zone Z at level 0, when an alarm device activates in Z, then Z becomes level 2 and all level-2 responses fire once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a level-3 response `lock-doors: [d1, d2]`, when triggered, then d1 and d2 are locked via the door system and pathfinding reflects it.
- AC-3 [unit] Given no alarm triggers for 5 sim minutes at level 2, when the decay rule runs, then Z drops to level 1 (never to 0 once an alarm has occurred).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a reserve creature already killed or knocked out by the player, when reinforcements are called, then it is not activated and no replacement is spawned.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a save while Z is at level 2, when loaded, then Z is at level 2 with its responses applied.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the stealth grey-box course, when the player is spotted and the alarm rung, then the course remains completable via at least one alternate route (scripted e2e path succeeds).

items.title: Build the stealth grey-box course covering every stealth input
items.description:
## Why
Stealth systems need one playable space that exercises light, sound, surfaces, doors, verticality and hiding for e2e tests and tuning playtests.

## What
A grey-box level `greybox/stealth-course` with labelled stations: light/dark gradient hall, surface strip (carpet/stone/gravel/creaky wood/water), door maze (open/closed/locked), vertical hall with rafters and ledges, hiding place gallery, distraction room, patrol yard with 3 fixture guards, alarm bell zone with reserve guards. Includes a baked navmesh, room/portal graph and patrol routes.

## Scope
- In: Level data, placeholder props, patrol routes, spawn points
- In: Console `tp station <n>`
- Out: Final dungeon content (E26)
- Out: Art

## Notes
Used by e09 e2e ACs, e09-infiltration-scenarios and e10 thief challenge.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the course, when loaded in the browser, then all 8 stations are reachable and no console errors appear.
- AC-2 [content] Given the course data, when validated, then navmesh, portal graph and patrol routes pass validation.
- AC-3 [integration] Given `tp station 3`, when entered, then the player is at the door maze start.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the course with all guards active, when measured on the reference machine (High), then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms.

items.title: Deterministic infiltration replay scenarios with asserted guard states
items.description:
## Why
Releases must be trusted without reading code. Scripted infiltrations with asserted guard states prove the stealth systems work together and stay working.

## What
A suite of ≥ 10 headless scenarios using the AI scenario harness on the stealth course layouts, each with a scripted player path and asserted guard states over time. Scenarios: shadow sneak (never above Suspicious), sprint on gravel (Suspicious ≤ 1 s), closed-door muffling, thrown distraction lure, break LOS and hide (guard ends Searching then postAlert Unaware), body discovery → Alerted, alarm → zone level 2, rafters crossing, hiding-place seen-enter, ally communication chain. Each records a state-hash sequence as a regression baseline.

## Scope
- In: Scenario files, baselines, CI job
- In: Readable failure timelines
- Out: Browser e2e (course e2e ACs)

## Notes
Scenarios reference fixture creatures only so bestiary tuning never breaks them.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the shadow-sneak scenario, when run, then no guard exceeds Suspicious for the full 60 s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the break-LOS scenario, when run, then the guard sequence is Combat → Searching → Unaware(postAlert) with the Searching phase starting within 5 s of LOS break.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the closed-door scenario, when the same noise is made with the door open vs closed, then the guard enters Suspicious only in the open case.
- AC-4 [integration] Given every scenario, when run twice, then state-hash sequences are identical to each other and to the committed baseline.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a deliberately broken rule (test-only flag doubling light weight), when the suite runs, then at least 3 scenarios fail (the suite actually detects regressions).
- AC-6 [perf] Given the full suite, when run in CI, then it completes in ≤ 30 s.

items.title: Stealth accessibility assists: slower detection, stronger cues
items.description:
## Why
Stealth must be approachable for players with different reaction speeds, hearing or vision without removing its systemic nature.

## What
As a player, I want stealth assist options so that I can enjoy infiltration at my own pace. Options: detection speed (50–150%), show indicators for unperceived agents, visual captions for noise events (“Footsteps — left”), stronger visibility gem contrast, extended hiding stagger window. Applied via the whitelisted stealth/AI tuning overrides.

## Scope
- In: Settings entries, override application, captions for noise events
- Out: Global accessibility framework (E31)

## Notes
Assists alter tuning inputs only; rules stay identical so scenario tests still hold at 100%.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given detection speed 50%, when a constant stimulus accumulates, then time to Suspicious doubles versus 100%.
- AC-2 [integration] Given noise captions on, when a 40 dB noise is perceived by the player from the left, then a caption with direction `left` appears within 100 ms.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an assist value outside the allowed range in settings storage, when loaded, then it clamps to the nearest bound.
- AC-4 [integration] Given all assists off, when the infiltration suite runs, then baselines are unchanged.

items.title: Playtest and tune stealth feel on the grey-box course
items.description:
## Why
A perfectly executed infiltration should feel as satisfying as a hard fight; only playtesting confirms that.

## What
Run 5 playtest sessions on the stealth course and first dungeon grey-box, record telemetry (detections, causes, time in each state, restarts), adjust tuning data, document changes in `docs/design/stealth-tuning-log.md`.

## Scope
- In: Sessions, telemetry capture, tuning edits, log
- Out: New mechanics (file new beads)

## Notes
Tuning changes that alter scenario baselines must update them in the same PR with rationale.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given 5 sessions, when players complete the course, then ≥ 4 of 5 rate stealth ≥ 4/5 for “I understood why I was seen”.
- AC-2 [integration] Given telemetry events for alert transitions, when exported, then each includes cause, state, and time-in-state fields.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the tuning log, when reviewed, then each change lists the metric that motivated it.

items.title: Define thief tool item data: lockpicks, throwables, smoke, traps
items.description:
## Why
Thief tools are data-driven items so shops, loot and progression can hand them out without code.

## What
Item definitions (in the inventory schema) for: lockpick set (durability), coin/pebble/bottle throwables (impact noise, breakable), smoke bomb, flash powder, noisemaker trap, tripwire kit, caltrops, rope, water flask (extinguish), sap/blackjack (non-lethal), disguise items referencing faction. Each carries world properties (weight, fragile, noise) and tags consumed by E10 features.

## Scope
- In: Item data files + tests
- In: Tags: `tool:lockpick`, `throwable`, `trap:*`, `disguise:<faction>`
- Out: Loot/shop placement (E18/E20)
- Out: Icons (asset beads)

## Notes
Placeholder icon ids: `icon-tool-lockpick`, `icon-throw-coin`, `icon-throw-bottle`, `icon-smoke-bomb`, `icon-trap-noisemaker`, `icon-trap-tripwire`, `icon-caltrops`, `icon-water-flask`, `icon-sap`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given each thief item file, when validated, then it passes the inventory item schema and carries its required tags.
- AC-2 [content] Given a throwable without an impact noise value, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a lockpick set with durability 10, when resolved, then durability is 10 and it stacks to max 5 sets.
- AC-4 [content] Given every thief item, when the content harness runs, then each has at least one automated test (spawn into inventory + use).

items.title: Throw objects to create noise distractions guards investigate
items.description:
## Why
Thrown distractions are the thief’s first verb in the progression ladder (Sneak → distractions → …) and a classic stealth tool.

## What
As a thief, I want to throw a coin or bottle so that guards look away or walk over to investigate. Any `throwable` item or physics object can be aimed (trajectory preview arc) and thrown; on impact it emits a noise event = item impact dB + surface offset; `fragile` items shatter (louder, leave shards as `glass-shards` surface). Guards perceive the propagated noise and investigate the perceived position. Thrown object remains in the world (anomaly if found near a post repeatedly — hook).

## Scope
- In: Throw aim + arc preview + release
- In: Impact noise via sound propagation + surface
- In: Pickup-able thrown objects (non-fragile)
- Out: Combat throwing damage (E04)
- Out: Arrows (E05)

## Notes
Uses physics objects for the throw; the noise rule is property-based (`throwable`, `fragile`), never item-specific.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a coin (impact 45 dB) landing on stone 10 m from a guard with threshold 30 dB, when propagated, then the guard receives a heard-noise stimulus and enters Suspicious.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a bottle tagged `fragile` landing, when it hits any surface, then it shatters, emits the fragile-break loudness and adds a `glass-shards` surface patch.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a coin landing on carpet, when propagated to the same guard, then perceived loudness is reduced by the carpet offset and the guard stays Unaware.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the distraction-room scenario, when the player throws a bottle behind a guard, then the guard turns and investigates the impact location within 2 s.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a throw into water, when it lands, then a `splash` noise kind is emitted and the object sinks (not retrievable unless shallow).
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box course, when the player aims, then a trajectory arc renders and the landing marker matches the actual landing point within 0.5 m.

items.title: Extinguish and relight light sources to reshape the shadows
items.description:
## Why
Extinguishing lights lets thieves create their own darkness, and any system that affects light (water, wind, frost magic) should work too.

## What
As a thief, I want to snuff candles and douse torches so that I can create shadows where I need them. Light sources with property `extinguishable` go out from: interact (pinch/snuff, quiet), any `wet`/water effect via element propagation (thrown water flask, rain), strong wind/gust effects, frost. `ignitable` light sources relight from any fire source. Light-field updates immediately; extinguishing emits a small noise and creates an anomaly (e09-anomaly-detection).

## Scope
- In: Light source state + property-based rules
- In: Interact snuff action
- In: Light-field update + anomaly record
- Out: Light-field implementation (e03-light-field)
- Out: Water arrows (E05) — works automatically via property

## Notes
Magical lights may be tagged non-extinguishable; that is data.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any `extinguishable` light within a water/wet effect volume, when the effect applies, then the light turns off and the light-field level at 2 m drops to the ambient value within 1 tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an `ignitable` unlit torch in contact with any fire source, when 0.5 s passes, then it relights.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a light tagged non-extinguishable, when water hits it, then it stays lit.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player snuffs a candle via interact, when complete, then a ≤ 15 dB noise is emitted and an anomaly `light-out` is registered for that light.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a guard walking past a torch the player extinguished, when perceived, then the guard enters Suspicious with cause `light-out`.

items.title: Backstabs and non-lethal takedowns on unaware targets
items.description:
## Why
Opportunistic combat is the thief’s combat fantasy: ambushes and takedowns reward patience and positioning.

## What
As a thief, I want to backstab or knock out an unaware enemy from behind so that a clean infiltration can thin the guard without a fight. Conditions: target alert state ∈ {Unaware, Suspicious}, player within rear arc (±60°) and 1.5 m, target does not perceive the player this think. Lethal backstab: damage multiplier from damage model (lethal on humanoids by default). Non-lethal (sap/choke): target becomes `unconscious` for a data-defined duration (default 10 min sim) unless woken. Creature schema flags (`immune-to-knockout` for undead/constructs, `no-backstab` for huge creatures) gate the verbs. Takedown emits noise (choke 20 dB, backstab 35 dB). Failed attempts (target turns) cause a scuffle: target enters Combat staggered.

## Scope
- In: Prompt availability, execution, outcomes, noise
- In: Creature flags gating
- In: Failure scuffle outcome
- Out: Environmental takedowns (e10-environmental-takedowns)
- Out: Animations (placeholder snaps)

## Notes
Unconscious bodies are carriable (e10-body-carry-hide) and anomalies (e09-anomaly-detection).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an Unaware humanoid and the player 1 m behind within 60°, when takedown is evaluated, then both backstab and knockout verbs are available.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same target in Investigating or higher, when evaluated, then no takedown verb is available.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature flagged `immune-to-knockout`, when evaluated, then only backstab is available.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a knockout, when executed, then the target is `unconscious` for 600 s sim and a 20 dB noise is emitted at its position.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the target perceives the player during the 0.5 s wind-up, when the takedown resolves, then it fails, the target enters Combat and is staggered for 0.8 s.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the patrol-yard scenario, when the player knocks out a guard out of sight of others, then the other guards remain Unaware.

items.title: Carry and hide unconscious or dead bodies
items.description:
## Why
Hiding bodies is how thieves cover their tracks; a body left in the light should cause the alarm the player earned.

## What
As a thief, I want to pick up and hide bodies so that patrols do not discover what I did. Pick up unconscious/dead humanoid-size creatures (size class limit), carry at reduced speed (−40%) and no sneak-sprint, higher visibility (+profile), drop or place into hiding places with `body-capacity` (chests, wardrobes, deep shadow, water). Placed bodies inside containers are invisible to anomaly detection; bodies in darkness depend on visibility. Unconscious creatures carried keep their wake timer.

## Scope
- In: Carry state, movement modifiers, drop/place
- In: Body containers
- In: Integration with anomaly detection
- Out: Ragdoll physics beyond placeholder (Related: physics/animation)
- Out: Looting bodies (e17 / E18)

## Notes
Dropping a body emits a thud noise scaled by surface (e.g. 35 dB on stone).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an unconscious guard, when the player picks it up, then player speed is ×0.6 and the visibility profile term increases by the configured amount.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player carrying a body, when placed into a container with body capacity 1, then the body is hidden and the container is full.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a body placed in a container, when a guard perceives the container, then no body anomaly is raised unless the guard opens it.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature larger than the carry size limit, when pickup is attempted, then it is refused with reason `too-heavy`.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the unconscious carried guard’s wake timer expires, when it wakes while carried, then it is dropped, enters Alerted and the player is staggered 0.5 s.

items.title: Spike: systemic lockpicking design that stays in the world
items.description:
## Why
The constitution prefers world systems over disconnected minigames. Lockpicking must keep the player in the world, exposed to guards and noise, while still involving skill.

## What
Time-box 1 day. Question: how can lockpicking be an in-world, interruptible action with a light skill layer (e.g. timing tension clicks while the camera stays third-person) instead of a full-screen minigame? Prototype 2 variants in the grey-box (A: timed hold with pin-click timing windows; B: pure duration by lock quality vs tool/skill with noise risk), evaluate readability, tension with nearby guards, accessibility (a no-skill option), and progression hooks. ADR with recommendation.

## Scope
- In: Two prototypes in `spikes/lockpicking/`
- In: ADR with lock data shape (quality, pins, noise per failure, jam chance)
- Out: Production lockpicking (e10-lockpicking)

## Notes
Must remain compatible with sorcerer/knight alternatives (Unlock spell, bashing) via the same lock component from e03-doors-locks-switches.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the ADR, when reviewed, then it records the choice, rejected alternatives, and a data shape for lock quality.
- AC-2 [manual] Given 3 internal testers, when trying both prototypes near a patrolling guard, then preferences and time-to-open are recorded in the ADR.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it specifies an accessibility mode that removes timing requirements.

items.title: Pick locks as an in-world, interruptible, noisy action
items.description:
## Why
Locked doors and chests are the thief’s signature alternate routes; picking them in the world while guards patrol creates tension.

## What
As a thief, I want to pick locks while staying aware of my surroundings so that opening a door is a tense, skilful choice rather than a menu. Implements the ADR: locks carry quality (1–5), pin count, jam chance; picking is an in-world action (player stays visible and hearable, camera third-person) consuming lockpick durability; skill layer per ADR with an accessibility no-timing mode. Failures emit small noises and may break a pick; jamming a lock makes it unpickable (bash/magic still work). Progression hooks raise max quality.

## Scope
- In: Lock component extension, pick action, noise, durability, jam
- In: In-world UI overlay (placeholder)
- In: Accessibility mode
- Out: Door/lock base mechanics (e03-doors-locks-switches)
- Out: Unlock spells/bashing (E06/E04, same component)

## Notes
Default noise per failed pin 18 dB; broken pick 25 dB.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a quality-2 lock and one lockpick set, when the pick action completes successfully, then the lock is unlocked and durability decreases by 1.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a failed pin attempt, when resolved, then an 18 dB noise event is emitted at the lock.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a lock jams (seeded chance), when evaluated, then further pick attempts are refused with reason `jammed` while other unlock methods still work.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player is attacked or moves > 0.5 m while picking, when resolved, then the action is interrupted and progress is lost.
- AC-5 [unit] Given lock quality above the player’s unlocked max, when the prompt is evaluated, then picking is not offered and the prompt says why.
- AC-6 [integration] Given accessibility no-timing mode, when picking a quality-3 lock, then it completes after the documented duration without input timing.
- AC-7 [e2e] Given the stealth grey-box door maze, when the player picks a locked door, then the door opens and the navmesh link becomes traversable.

items.title: Pickpocket and plant items on creatures from behind
items.description:
## Why
Pickpocketing creates emergent solutions: steal a key instead of picking a lock, plant evidence, lift a guard’s disguise pass.

## What
As a thief, I want to lift items from, or plant items on, unaware creatures so that I can solve problems without violence. Available when target is Unaware/Suspicious, not perceiving the player, within 1.2 m behind/side arc. Opens a compact in-world list of visible pockets (creature inventory items flagged `pocketable`). Each attempt takes time by item weight; success chance falls with target awareness and item weight; a failed attempt raises target awareness sharply (Alerted if it turns and sees you). Theft is recorded (disposition/faction events for witnesses).

## Scope
- In: Pickpocket and plant actions, success model, witness events
- In: Creature inventory integration
- In: Compact UI (placeholder)
- Out: Creature loot tables (e18-loot-tables)
- Out: Crime/bounty (Related: crime system)

## Notes
Success probability formula documented in tuning data; seeded RNG.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an Unaware guard with a `pocketable` key, when the player attempts from behind at 1 m, then the item transfers on success and the attempt takes the weight-scaled duration.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a failed attempt, when resolved, then the target’s awareness increases by the configured spike and it turns toward the player.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a witness guard perceives the theft, when resolved, then a `witnessed-theft` event fires applying disposition and faction modifiers.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a target with no pocketable items, when the prompt is evaluated, then the verb is offered but the list shows “Nothing to take” (still allows planting).
- AC-5 [unit] Given the target walks out of range mid-attempt, when resolved, then the attempt cancels without a transfer or awareness spike.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the player plants an item on a guard, when saved and loaded, then the guard’s inventory contains the planted item.

items.title: Climb tagged surfaces, ledges and ropes with stamina
items.description:
## Why
Climbing is how the thief reaches the window, the rooftop and the rafters — the class-specific alternate route.

## What
As a thief, I want to climb rough walls, vines, ladders and ropes so that I can take routes other classes cannot. Surfaces with property `climbable` (with difficulty) allow climbing; ledges allow shimmy and mantle; placed ropes (from items) create temporary climbable lines. Climbing drains stamina per difficulty; running out causes a fall (noise + damage by height). Class/progression gates higher difficulties. Climbing is quiet (−10 dB vs walk) but you are silhouetted on walls (contrast rule).

## Scope
- In: Climb state machine on top of controller climb hooks
- In: Stamina drain + fall
- In: Rope placement creating climbable volume + nav link for climbers
- Out: Core controller physics (e02-player-controller)
- Out: Climbing animations (placeholders)

## Notes
Climb routes also produce off-mesh links usable by climber creatures (e11-navigation).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a `climbable` difficulty-2 wall and a thief with max climb difficulty 3, when climb is initiated, then the player enters Climbing state.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a knight with max climb difficulty 1, when attempting the same wall, then climb is refused with a reason prompt.
- AC-3 [unit] Given stamina reaches 0 while climbing 4 m up, when the tick runs, then the player falls, takes fall damage per curve and a landing noise is emitted.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a rope placed on an anchor point, when complete, then a climbable volume and an off-mesh climb link exist until the rope is retrieved.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the stealth course vertical hall, when the player climbs to the rafters, then the player stands on the rafter platform within 10 s of input with no console errors.

items.title: Disguises that fool factions until behaviour gives you away
items.description:
## Why
Disguises are a later thief verb in the progression ladder and create social infiltration moments.

## What
As a thief, I want to wear a faction’s uniform so that I can walk among guards if I behave. Equipping a `disguise:<faction>` item makes that faction’s members treat the player as `disguised` instead of intruder: sight stimuli accumulate a separate suspicion meter driven by proximity (< 3 m), suspicious behaviour (running, crouching, climbing, being in restricted zones, being seen committing crimes, carrying bodies), and observer traits (officers and dogs see through faster; `sees-through-disguise` flag). Suspicion full → disguise blown for that zone (remembered).

## Scope
- In: Disguise state, per-observer suspicion rules, restricted zone data, blown-state memory
- Out: Dialogue with disguised player (E22)
- Out: Uniform art (placeholder recolour)

## Notes
Suspicion rules are tuning data; restricted zones are level regions.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player wears a disguise of faction A and walks at normal speed 8 m from an A guard in a public zone, when 30 s pass, then the guard remains Unaware.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same player sprints within 3 m, when evaluated, then disguise suspicion accumulates at the running rate and the guard enters Suspicious within 3 s.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an observer flagged `sees-through-disguise`, when it perceives the player, then the disguise is ignored.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the disguise is blown in zone Z, when the player re-enters Z still disguised, then Z’s guards treat the player as an intruder.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a faction B guard, when perceiving the player in faction A disguise, then normal intruder rules apply.

items.title: Place traps: noisemakers, tripwires and caltrops
items.description:
## Why
Traps let the thief shape the battlefield ahead of time — dirty tricks and disengagement are the thief combat fantasy.

## What
As a thief, I want to place traps so that I can lure, slow or warn about enemies. Place trap items on valid surfaces with a placement preview: noisemaker (timed or triggered noise event), tripwire (trigger volume between two anchors → alarm noise for player, or trip/stagger), caltrops (slow + damage zone, noise when stepped). Traps are world objects with properties (flammable tripwire burns, etc.), perceivable by AI (visibility check); perceiving an armed trap makes AI avoid it and become Suspicious.

## Scope
- In: Placement preview + validity, trap objects, trigger logic via e03-triggers
- In: AI avoidance of perceived traps (nav cost)
- Out: World/dungeon traps and disarming (e10-trap-disarm)
- Out: Trap art (placeholders)

## Notes
Creatures can trigger player traps; the player can too (friendly fire).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a caltrops item and a flat valid surface, when placed, then a slow zone (×0.5 speed) with damage 2/s exists at the location.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a placement on a slope > 30° or in water, when previewed, then placement is invalid with reason.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a tripwire between two anchors, when any creature crosses it, then its trigger fires once and it becomes spent.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a guard perceives an armed caltrops zone, when pathing, then its path avoids the zone if an alternative exists and it enters Suspicious.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a tripwire tagged `flammable` in a fire volume, when 1 s passes, then it burns and is removed without triggering.

items.title: Detect and disarm world traps; failures trigger them
items.description:
## Why
Triggered traps should create new situations rather than reloads; spotting and disarming them is thief expertise.

## What
As a thief, I want to notice and disarm pressure plates, tripwires and dart traps so that I can open safe routes — and accept the chaos when I fail. Traps have a `concealment` value; the player perceives them via a proximity/light-based check (thieves have a bonus; sneaking slower improves it) which reveals a subtle highlight. Disarm is an in-world timed action (like lockpicking) with a failure chance by trap quality; failure triggers the trap. Disarmed traps can be picked up (become placeable items where data allows).

## Scope
- In: Trap detection check, reveal highlight, disarm action, fail-trigger
- In: Salvage to item
- Out: Trap mechanics/effects themselves (e03-triggers / e03-doors-locks-switches)
- Out: Dungeon trap placement (E26)

## Notes
Detection uses light-field at trap position: dark traps are harder to spot.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a trap with concealment 0.5 in light 0.8, when a thief sneaks within 3 m, then it is detected within 1 s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same trap in light 0.1, when a knight walks within 3 m, then it is not detected.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a disarm attempt that fails (seeded), when resolved, then the trap triggers its normal effect.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a successfully disarmed pressure plate, when a creature steps on it, then nothing triggers.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a disarmed tripwire, when salvaged, then a tripwire kit item is added to inventory.

items.title: Smoke bombs and flash powder break line of sight for escapes
items.description:
## Why
Escape tools turn failed stealth into a chase instead of a death — the thief’s disengagement fantasy.

## What
As a thief, I want to throw a smoke bomb so that I can break line of sight and slip away. Smoke bomb creates a gas volume (via element propagation, drifts and dissipates over 12 s) tagged `occlusion: partial:0.1` for LOS; creatures inside have sight disabled and cough (noise). Flash powder: instant stun for creatures facing it within 5 m (sight-dependent — blind/life-sense creatures unaffected). Losing LOS feeds LKP rules, so guards search where you vanished.

## Scope
- In: Smoke gas volume + LOS occlusion + dissipation
- In: Flash stun rule by sense profile
- In: Integration with memory/LKP
- Out: Gas propagation engine (e03-element-propagation)
- Out: VFX art (placeholders)

## Notes
Smoke is a gas: a Gust effect should clear it via the same gas rules (property-based).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a smoke volume between guard and player, when LOS is queried, then visible fraction ≤ 0.1.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a smoke volume, when 12 s pass without wind, then it has dissipated and LOS is restored.
- AC-3 [unit] Given flash powder within 5 m and a guard facing it, when detonated, then the guard is stunned 3 s; a creature without sight senses is not stunned.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a Combat guard chasing the player, when the player throws smoke and runs 10 m sideways, then the guard enters Searching with LKP at the smoke cloud, not the player’s position.
- AC-5 [unit] Given any gas-clearing wind effect through the smoke volume, when applied, then the volume moves/dissipates per gas rules.

items.title: Silent movement unlocks: soft steps, muffled gear, shadow dash
items.description:
## Why
Anti-grind rule: progression unlocks verbs, not +12%. Silent movement should grow into new capabilities.

## What
As a thief, I want to unlock ways to move more silently so that I can take bolder routes. Capability unlocks via the progression model: `soft-step` (sneak gait ignores creaky-board creaks and gravel offset), `muffled-gear` (equipment noise halved while sneaking), `shadow-dash` (short burst of sneak-speed movement at walk noise while in light ≤ 0.2). Each is a data-defined modifier applied to the footstep/visibility rules.

## Scope
- In: Three capability modifiers as data + rule hooks
- Out: Progression UI and unlock sources (E19)

## Notes
Modifiers alter inputs to e09-footstep-noise and e09-visibility-model only; rules stay pure.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given `soft-step` unlocked, when sneaking on `wood-creaky`, then no creak event is ever emitted over 1,000 seeded steps.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `muffled-gear` and equipment noise +10 dB, when sneaking, then the footstep includes +5 dB equipment noise.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `shadow-dash` in light 0.5, when activated, then it is refused because light exceeds 0.2.
- AC-4 [unit] Given no unlocks, when evaluated, then footstep results equal the base rule exactly.

items.title: Lean around corners and peek through keyholes
items.description:
## Why
Information is the thief’s currency; peeking lets players scout routines before committing.

## What
As a thief, I want to lean around corners and peek through keyholes so that I can scout without exposing myself. Lean shifts camera and exposes only the head sample point to LOS (reduced visibility). Keyhole peek on doors with a `keyhole` flag gives a narrow view of the next room with the player fully hidden from that room.

## Scope
- In: Lean input + camera offset + LOS sample override
- In: Keyhole peek interaction
- Out: Camera system (e02-camera)

## Notes
During lean, only the head sample point counts for LOS (1 of 4).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player leaning, when LOS is queried by an observer, then only the head sample point is considered.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a door without a keyhole, when interaction options are built, then peek is not offered.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a keyhole peek, when active, then the camera renders from the keyhole position and visibility to observers in the other room is 0.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player is attacked while peeking, when damage applies, then peek ends immediately.

items.title: Environmental takedowns: drop, push and douse via world properties
items.description:
## Why
The progression ladder ends at environmental takedowns; the world itself becomes the thief’s weapon, and it must be systemic.

## What
As a thief, I want to drop a chandelier, cut a hanging load or push a crate from a ledge onto an enemy so that the world does my work. Any object with `suspended` property released (cut rope, shot chain, lever) falls under physics; impact damage = f(mass, fall height) via the damage model. Deaths/knockouts caused by environment are tagged `accident` so witnesses raise lower suspicion (Suspicious/Investigating instead of Alerted) unless they perceived the player causing it.

## Scope
- In: Falling-object damage rule by mass/height
- In: Accident attribution + AI response weights
- Out: Specific set-pieces (E26 content)
- Out: Rope cutting by arrows (E05, works via property)

## Notes
Property-based: never "chandelier" in rules.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any object tagged `suspended` with mass 80 kg released from 5 m onto a creature, when impact resolves, then damage equals the documented mass×height curve.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature killed by a falling object with no witness perceiving the player within 3 s, when attributed, then the event is tagged `accident`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a witness to an `accident`, when evaluated, then it enters Investigating (not Alerted).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a witness perceived the player releasing the object, when evaluated, then it enters Alerted with the player LKP.

items.title: Grey-box thief infiltration challenge with multiple scripted routes
items.description:
## Why
Milestone m2 requires the thief fantasy proven in grey-box; a perfect infiltration must feel as good as a hard fight.

## What
A grey-box vault infiltration `greybox/thief-vault`: guarded courtyard, lit halls, a locked vault with a key carried by a patrolling guard, climbable exterior wall, alarm bell, hiding places. At least 3 distinct solution routes (pickpocket key; climb + pick window lock; distraction + extinguish + takedown), each covered by a scripted e2e/scenario test. Records a “ghost” (never detected) flag on completion.

## Scope
- In: Level data, routes, scripted solution tests, completion flag
- Out: Final dungeon (E26)
- Out: Art

## Notes
Fixture creatures only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given route A (pickpocket), when the scripted scenario runs, then the vault opens and no guard exceeds Suspicious.
- AC-2 [integration] Given route B (climb + lockpick window), when run, then the vault is reached and the completion flag is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given route C (distract + extinguish + takedown), when run, then the vault opens with one unconscious guard hidden and no alarm.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a scripted failure (player spotted in the courtyard), when run, then the alarm escalates the zone and the scripted escape via smoke + hiding place still completes the level.
- AC-5 [manual] Given 3 playtesters, when completing the vault undetected, then ≥ 2 rate satisfaction ≥ 4/5.
